The sūrah opens with a call that is also a claim, and the first words put the whole of its teaching under one heading: “O believers, Honour your obligations”. The obligations are the pledges that faith has laid on the one who accepts it, and the order matters, because the demand comes before any detail of what is lawful and what is not. From that general claim the verse moves to a gift, since “All grazing livestock has been made lawful to you” names the animals people raise and keep, the grazing herds of their daily use, and the permission is put as something already settled rather than something to be earned. The gift is then given an edge, because “except what is hereby announced to you and hunting while on pilgrimage, Indeed” leaves outside it an animal whose description the verses that follow set out, and game taken while the pilgrim is still under the sacred restriction, so the permission is a rule with known limits and not an open door. The word used for hunting is the catching of wild game, and the exception is announced here rather than left to be discovered by the reader. The verse closes by naming the ground of the whole matter, “Allah commands what He wills”, which places the lawful and the unlawful on the command of God and not on the taste or the reasoning of the people addressed. That is the shape the rest of the passage keeps: a claim on the believer, a permission, a limit, and the authority that stands behind all three. Nothing here is left as a suggestion, and nothing is left without a reason, since the verses that follow go straight from the claim to the detail of what may be eaten, what may not, and who is answerable for the difference. The address is to people who have already accepted the message, so the claim is made of them and not of strangers, and the passage is a reminder of what they have already bound themselves to rather than a new burden laid on them from outside.

**The obligations and the covenant that binds.**

(1. O you who believe! Fulfill (your) obligations. Lawful to you (for food) are all the beasts of cattle except that which will be announced to you (herein), game (also) being unlawful when you assume Ihram. Verily, Allah commands that which He wills.)(2. O you who believe! Violate not the sanctity of the symbols of Allah, nor of the Sacred Month, nor of the Hady brought for sacrifice, nor the garlands, nor the people coming to the Sacred House (Makkah), seeking the bounty and good pleasure of their Lord. But when you finish the Ihram, then hunt, and let not the hatred of some people in (once) stopping you from Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah) lead you to transgression. Help you one another in Al-Birr and At-Taqwa, but do not help one another in sin and transgression. And have Taqwa of Allah. Verily, Allah is severe in punishment.) (O ye who believe! Fulfil your undertakings): '(O ye who believe! Fulfil your undertakings) fulfil the pledges that are between you and Allah or between you and other people; it is also said that this means: fulfil the obligations which have been made obligatory upon you and which you accepted on the Day of the Covenant and in this Book. Some say that it refers to the Covenant of Allah under which His created beings are bound to believe in and obey Him, or they refer to pledges Allah has taken from His created beings regarding His revealed injunctions of things lawful and unlawful. This is what has been reported from Sayyidna Ibn Abbas Others say that here it means the contracts people enter into with each other, such as, the Contract of Marriage and the Contract of Buying and Selling. (O you who believe! Fulfill (your) obligations.) "Refers to the covenants, meaning, what Allah permitted, prohibited, ordained and set limits for in the Qur'an.

**The beasts of cattle made lawful to you.**

Lawful to you is the beast of the flocks camels cattle and sheep and goats to eat after slaughtering them except that which is now being recited to you as forbidden in the verse below Forbidden to you are carrion…Q. 53; the exceptive clause here is a discontinuous one but may also be continuous; the forbidding concerns that which has succumbed to death and the like; game not being lawful to you when you are on pilgrimage hurum means muhrimūn; ghayra ‘not’ is in the accusative as it introduces a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the pronoun lakum ‘to you’. (The beast of cattle is made lawful unto you (for food) you have a legal dispensation to eat of the meat of game such as wild oxen, wild camels and gazelles (except that which is announced unto you) except that which is recited to you in this surah, (game being unlawful when ye are on pilgrimage) or in the Sacred Precinct. Allah has permitted for you, out of His mercy, livestock animals (camels, cattle, sheep and goats), except those the prohibition of which have been read to you and the land game that He has prohibited you from in the state of sanctity during the pilgrimage of Hajj or Umrah. So, the meaning of the verse comes to be that eight kinds of domestic animals have been made lawful for you.' Under the discussion about the word, al- uqud', you have already read a little earlier that it includes all kinds of contracts. " Here, Allah states, "Just as We allowed the meat of cattle in all conditions and circumstances, then do not hunt game when in the state of Ihram, for this is the decision of Allah, Who is the Most Wise in all that He commands and forbids.

**The exception announced in the verse.**

(except that which will be announced to you (herein),) 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas said that it refers to, "The flesh of dead animals, blood and the meat of swine. It was also reported that the meaning here is, "We have allowed for you all types of cattle in all circumstances, except what We excluded herewith for the one hunting game while in the state of Ihram. He, in His grace, makes what is good and pure openly lawful for human consumption, things which leave no ill effects on physical health and moral strength. The present sentence is referring to this particular pledge when it says that Allah has made the cattle lawful for you and they can be eaten after having been slaughtered in accordance with the Islamic manner. So, in the light of this verse, strict adherence to all permissible provisions and conditions which have been mutually agreed upon is mandatory and all parties must observe and fulfill these.

**The command that decides the lawful and the unlawful.**

Verily God decrees whatever He desires in the way of making things lawful or otherwise and there can be no objection thereto. He makes lawful and prohibits what He wills whether you are in a state of ritual consecration or not. Allah decides to permit and prohibit as He wills in accordance with His wisdom. Towards the end of the verse, it was said: ‌ which means that Allah Almighty ordains what He wills. So, take what has been made lawful there as lawful forever and take what has been made unlawful there as unlawful forever. Rather than do something like that, believers must eat from animals Allah Almighty has made lawful to eat under the Law given by Him. The Creator and Master who has made all these life forms is also the One who has formulated, in His perfect wisdom and insight, the law that the lower form shall be the sustenance of the higher.

**What the call, the honor and the allusion carry.**

It is narrated that Jaʿfar ibn MuḤammad said that these words have four traits through which the Lord of the Worlds honored and caressed the community. One is that they are a call, second an intimation, third an allusion, and fourth a bearing witness. O is a call, you is an intimation, who is an allusion, and have faith is a bearing witness. The call is an honor, the intimation of mercy, the allusion to love, and the bearing witness to recognition. "He called them before He made them appear, and He named them before He saw them. " They were in the concealment of nonexistence when He called them to honor.

**What the obligation lays on the animals and people.**

Animals have not been so obligated, other-wise Allah has given to every animal sense and awareness within the limits of its needs - even to all trees and rocks, for that matter. How then, without sense, would it have ever recognized its creator and master and how would it have, thus, been able to engage in the act of glorifying Allah? This is the reason why human beings have been obligated to observe the percepts and injunctions revealed for them. So, the meaning of the verse comes to be that eight kinds of domestic animals have been made lawful for you.' Under the discussion about the word, al- uqud', you have already read a little earlier that it includes all kinds of contracts. He, in His grace, makes what is good and pure openly lawful for human consumption, things which leave no ill effects on physical health and moral strength. In the matter of God or His subjects he has taken it upon himself not to act independently but according to God’s commandments. He should have as food only those things that God has permitted and give up eating those things which God has forbidden. If on some occasions even permitted things are forbidden, as is evident from orders applicable while in the state of ihram or during sacred months, he should willingly accept this. Ibn Jarir said that, "Ithm means abandoning what Allah has ordained, while transgression means overstepping the limits that Allah set in your religion, along with overstepping what Allah has ordered concerning yourselves and others.

2.text:
The verse gathers the honours of the pilgrimage and rules out treating any of them lightly: “O believers, Do not violate Allah’s rituals of pilgrimage”, and the word for rituals covers the rites and the places that God has marked as sacred. “the sacred months” are named next, the months in which fighting and violation were held back, and then “the sacrificial animals”, the beasts driven to the House for offering. The list continues with “the offerings decorated with garlands”, animals marked with wreaths so that anyone who sees them knows they are consecrated and leaves them alone. Then come the people themselves, “nor those pilgrims on their way to the Sacred House seeking their Lord’s bounty and pleasure”, so the protection extends to travellers whose journey is a request for provision and for acceptance, and the two words at the end name what they hope for, gain and good pleasure together. The verse then lifts the restriction at the right moment, since “When pilgrimage has ended, you are allowed to hunt”, and the permission is tied to the ending of the sacred state and not to the passing of a month. What follows is the moral the passage is built on: “Do not let the hatred of a people who once barred you from the Sacred Mosque provoke you to transgress”, which addresses a real grievance, since those people had turned the believers away from the House, and it rules out answering a wrong with a wrong. From that the verse moves to the company a believer keeps, “Cooperate with one another in goodness and righteousness, and do not cooperate in sin and transgression”, a pair of commands that make the community itself the field of the ruling. “And be mindful of Allah” then carries the whole set of duties back to the one who sees them, and “Surely Allah is severe in punishment” closes on the warning that gives the prohibition its weight. Care for the pilgrim, restraint towards the enemy and care in choosing whom one helps belong to a single theme here, the honour of what God has made sacred and the discipline of the people who honour it.

**The sacred signs and the months of pilgrimage.**

(O ye who believe! Profane not Allah's monuments) do not make lawful the abstention from all of Allah's rites (nor the Sacred Month) nor attacking people in the Sacred Month (nor the offerings) nor the taking of offerings which are made to the House (nor the garlands) nor the taking of the garlands which are hung by the advent of the Sacred Month, (nor those repairing to the Sacred House) nor attacking those who head for Allah's Sacred House, i.e. the pilgrims of al-Yamamah-the clan of the idolater Bakr Ibn Wa'il-and the traders of the idolater Shurayh Ibn Dabi'ah, (seeking the grace) provision (and pleasure of Allah) by means of the pilgrimage. O you who believe do not profane God’s sacraments sha‘ā’ir is the plural of sha‘īra that is the ritual ceremonies of the religion by hunting game while you are on pilgrimage nor the sacred month by fighting in it nor the offering that is the boon offered in the Meccan Sanctuary by interfering with it nor the garlands qalā’id is the plural of qilāda and these made from the trees around the Sanctuary were placed around it the offering to protect it in other words do not interfere with these offerings or with those who place them; nor violate the sanctity of those repairing those heading to the Sacred House by fighting them who are seeking bounty provision from their Lord through commerce and His beatitude by resorting to Him as they the Meccans pagans falsely claimed this was abrogated by the barā’a verse of sūrat al-Tawba Q. 94. (nor of the Sacred Month,) for you are required to respect and honor the Sacred Month and to refrain from what Allah forbade during it, such as fighting. (The division of time has returned as it was when Allah created the Heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, four of which are sacred: Three are in succession, (they are:) Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and (the fourth is) Rajab of (the tribe of) Mudar which comes between Jumada (Ath-Thaniyah) and Sha'ban.)

**The animals brought for sacrifice and the garlands.**

(nor of the Hady brought for sacrifice, nor the garlands,) means, do not abandon the practice of bringing the Hady (sacrificial animals) to the Sacred House, as this ritual is a form of honoring the symbols of Allah. This way, it will be known that these animals are intended to be offered as Hady at the Ka'bah, and thus those who might intend some harm to them would refrain from doing so. Do not violate the sacrificial animal by siezing it or preventing it from reaching its place of sacrifice. Also not permissible was stopping sacrificial animals from reaching the Haram or taking them away forcibly.

**Those on their way to the Sacred House.**

Likewise, those who are heading towards the Sacred House seeking the bounty and good pleasure of Allah, must not be stopped, prevented, or frightened away from entering the Sacred House. (and pleasure.) Ibn 'Abbas said that the word 'pleasure' in the Ayah refers to, "seeking Allah's pleasure by their Hajj." 'Ikrimah, As-Suddi and Ibn Jarir mentioned that this Ayah was revealed concerning Al-Hutam bin Hind Al-Bakri, who had raided the cattle belonging to the people of Al-Madīnah. When the Muslims wanted to get him, Allah, exalted is He, revealed (O ye who believe! Profane not Allah's monuments), by monuments here is meant that which is offered for Allah, even if those who offer it profess a religion other than Islam . As for the disbelievers who have donned the Ihram garments and who, in their estimation, have embarked on their pilgrimage to seek the good pleasure of Allah Almighty (though, because of their disbelief, this is a mistaken notion, yet) the sanctity of the signs of Allah demands that they should not be confronted in any way.

**Hunting after the sacred state ends.**

But when you are discharged from pilgrimage inviolability then hunt for game a command denoting permission. (But when you finish the Ihram, then hunt,) When you end your Ihram, it is permitted for you to hunt game, which was prohibited for you during Ihram. (But when ye have left the sacred territory) after the days of Tashriq, (then go hunting (if ye will) if you will, go hunt wild game. Stay away from those things that are prohibited when you are in the state of pilgrim sanctity, such as wearing your normal clothing, and those things that are prohibited within the Sanctuary, such as hunting.

**The hatred that must not provoke a wrong.**

And let not hatred read shana’ānu or shan’ānu of a people that because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque cause you to commit aggression against them by killing them or otherwise. (And let not your hatred of a folk) the hatred of the people of Makkah (who (once) stopped your going to the Inviolable Place of Worship) on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah (seduce you) drive you (to transgress) against the pilgrims of the clan of Bakr Ibn Wa'il; (but help ye one another unto righteousness) acts of obedience (and pious duty) shunning transgressions. (And let not the enmity and hatred of others make you avoid justice. Be just: that is nearer to piety,)[5:8] which commands: do not be driven by your hatred for some people into abandoning justice, for justice is ordained for everyone, in all situations. But this type of revengeful, inimical action is not legitimate in the eyes of God, even if it were in retaliation for being prevented from performing the pilgrimage to the Sacred Mosque in Makkah.

**Cooperating in goodness, and where it stops.**

Help one another to righteousness by doing that to which you were enjoined and piety by refraining from what you have been forbidden; do not help one another ta‘āwanū one of the two original tā’ letters in tata‘āwanū has been omitted to sin acts of disobedience and enmity transgression of God’s bounds. Incidentally, this cooperation is not limited to the life of the world of our experience, it is also needed in the stages from death to burial – even beyond, when one remains depending upon those he left behind and who may pray for his forgiveness and do things the reward of which keeps reaching him after his death. A practical demonstration of this Qur'anic classification was visible during the battles of Badr, Uhud, Ahzab and Hunayn when a blood brother who elected to stay away from the obedience of Allah and His Rasul found that his bond of mutual coopera-tion with his believing brother stood severed and he could no longer escape the stroke of his believing brother's sword. As for the one who invites people to the path of error or sin, he or she will be earning the same amount of sin fully equal to the sins of all those who got involved with the filth of sin because of the inviter to sin - without any decrease in the count of such sins. It is the most difficult task in the present world to support those who are on the right path and ignore those who are not on the right path as they have all the wordly glories by their side. (Help not one another unto sin) contraventions (and transgression) against the pilgrims of the clan of Bakr Ibn Wa'il, (but keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in that which He has commanded and prohibited you. The text then prohibits the violation of the sanctity of those who have left their homes to embark on a journey to al-Masjid al-Haram with the intention of performing Hajj - for their purpose on this journey is to seek the blessing and pleasure of their Lord.

3.text:
The verse sets out what is forbidden, and it does so in a rising order. “Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, and swine” names the three that need no description, an animal that died of itself, blood poured out, and the pig. Then come the ways an animal may be killed without a proper slaughter: “what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah”, which takes the act out from under the name it must be done under, then “what is killed by strangling, beating, a fall”, “or by being gored to death”, each of them a death by violence or accident rather than by the knife. “what is partly eaten by a predator unless you slaughter it” brings in the animal torn by a wild beast, and the exception inside the phrase keeps the rule workable, since a quick slaughter before it dies makes it lawful. “and what is sacrificed on altars” covers what was offered to stones and idols, and “You are also forbidden to draw lots for decisions” puts beside the list of foods a practice of deciding by arrows, which the verse treats as the same kind of error, and it names that plainly: “This is all evil”. The passage then turns from the list to what the day itself brought: “Today the disbelievers have given up all hope of undermining your faith”, and the completion of the religion is announced in that setting. So the believers hear “So do not fear them, fear Me”, and then the words that give the sūrah its weight, “Today I have perfected your faith for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your way”. The three statements sit together, a faith brought to its completion, a favour brought to its end, and a way named for the people who walk it. The last lines keep the door of mercy open: “But whoever is compelled by extreme hunger, not intending to sin, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful”, so the prohibition is not a trap for the desperate, and the intent of the heart is named as the thing that decides. The foods, the slaughter, the divining, the day of completion and the concession for hunger are held together in one passage on purpose, and the reader is meant to take them as a single instruction rather than as separate rulings.

**What is forbidden of the dead and the blood.**

Al-Maytah (the dead animals), blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been slaughtered as a sacrifice for other than Allah, and that which has been killed by strangling, or by a violent blow, or by a headlong fall, or by the goring of horns and that which has been (partly) eaten by a wild animal unless you are able to slaughter it (before its death) - and that which is sacrificed (slaughtered) on An-Nusub (stone altars). (Forbidden unto you (for food) are carrion) He says: eating carrion is forbidden for you because He has commanded that it be immolated (and blood) which is shed (and swine flesh, and that which hath been dedicated unto any other than Allah) in purpose, (and the strangled) that which is strangled with a rope until it dies, (and the dead through beating) the beast beaten by a piece of wood until it dies, (and the dead through falling from a height) or in a well and which dies as a consequence, (and that which has been killed by (the goring of) horns, and the devoured of wild beasts) as a prey, (saving that which ye make lawful) except that which you find on the verge of dying and make it lawful by immolating it, (and that which hath been immolated unto idols. And (forbidden is it) that you swear by the divining arrows) He says: He has also forbidden you from spilled blood; pig’s meat; an animal on which other than the name of Allah was taken at the time of slaughter; an animal that was strangled or beaten to death, or one that fell from a high place; or an animal that was gored by another animal and an animal that was hunted by a predator, such as a lion, tiger or wolf, unless you reach any of these animals while they are alive and you slaughter them – in which case they will be lawful for you. Forbidden to you is carrion that is the consumption of it and blood that is what has been spilt as mentioned in sūrat al-An‘ām Q. 6145 and the flesh of swine and what has been hallowed to other than God in that it was sacrificed in the name of something other than Him and the beast strangled to death and the beast beaten down to death and the beast fallen from a height to its death and the beast gored to death by another and what beasts of prey have devoured of such animals — except for what you have sacrificed duly catching it while it still breathes life and then sacrificing it — and what has been sacrificed in the name of idols nusub is the plural of nusāb and that you apportion that is that you demand an oath or a ruling through the divining of arrows azlām the plural of zalam or zulam which is a qidh ‘a small arrow’ without feathers or a head. Forbidden to you are carrion and blood, the flesh of swine, that which has been offered up to other than God, the strangled, the beaten down, the fallen, the gored, what has been eaten by predators-except what you slaughter-what is sacrificed on stone alters, and that which you al lot by divining arrows-that is ungodliness.

**The ways an animal may be killed.**

(You can use what makes blood flow and you can eat what is slaughtered with the Name of Allah. But do not use teeth or claws (in slaughtering). I will tell you why, as for teeth, they are bones, and claws are used by Ethiopians for slaughtering.)" Allah said next,. Therefore, the Prophet made a distinction between killing the animal with the sharp edge of an arrow or a hunting stick, and rendered it lawful, and what is killed by the broad side of an object, and rendered it unlawful because it was beaten to death. For the same reason, in the Islamic law, the consumption of all types of dead animals is also forbidden, because the blood of a dead animal immediately gets absorbed in its flesh. The reason why this has been mentioned in the context of unlawful animals is that small groups of pagan Arabs used to have a joint slaughter of a camel or some other animal but, rather than divide up shares from the meat to all participants in accordance with the num-ber of shares originally subscribed to, they would decide it by drawing these arrows.

**Drawing lots and the arrows of divination.**

(Forbidden) also is to make decisions with Al-Azlam (arrows) that is Fisq (disobedience and sin). He has also prohibited you from drawing lots to know whether something is destined for you or not, or to use as a means of making a decision when intending to do something or not. (This is sin) which follows immediately after this injunction means that this method of divination or determining of shares is an act of sin which leads people astray.

**The day the faith was perfected.**

Today I have perfected your religion for you that is its rulings and obligations after this verse nothing about what is lawful or unlawful was revealed and I have completed My favour upon you by perfecting it your religion but it is also said by effecting their safe entry into Makkah; and I have approved chosen Islam for you as religion. (This day) the day of the pilgrimage (have I perfected your religion for you) I have elucidated to you the prescriptions of your religion: the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and the prohibitions (and completed My favour unto you) I have completed My blessing upon you in that, after today, no idolater will ever gather with you in 'Arafat, Mina, in the circumambulation around the Ka'bah, and in the coming and going between al-Safa and al-Marwah, (and have chosen for you as religion al-Islam. (This day) the day of the greater pilgrimage, the farewell pilgrimage (are those who disbelieve) the unbelievers of Makkah (in despair of your religion) in despair of you religion reverting to theirs after you left their religion and its laws; (so fear them not) in relation to following the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and opposing them (fear Me!) if you abstain from following Muhammad and his religion and follow them. Thus, 'Perfection of Faith' tells us that the purpose of sending Divine Law and the injunctions of Faith into this world stands fulfilled and perfected today; and 'Completion of Blessing' means that Muslims do not have to depend on anyone any-more. This is because 'Din' (Faith) is demonstrated by what the members of the Community do while the consummation of 'Ni'mah' (Blessing) is directly from Al-mighty Allah (Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir). This has been explained by Imam Raghib al-Isfahan' in his Mufradat al-Qur'an by saying that the 'Ikmal and TakmIl' (Perfection) of something means that the purpose and objective behind it has been accomplished (perfection of something carries exactly the same sense in English, specially at a time when spoken of, as 'al-yowm' (today) in the verse al-ready indicates).

**The concession for extreme hunger.**

But whoever is constrained by emptiness by hunger to consume some of what has been forbidden him and consumes it not inclining purposely to sin to an act of disobedience — then God is Forgiving to him for what he has consumed Merciful to him by permitting it to him in contrast to the one who purposely inclines to sin that is the one actively engaged in it such as a waylayer or a criminal for whom such consumption is forbidden. But as for him who is forced by severe hunger, with no inclination to sin (such can eat these above mentioned animals), then surely, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. Towards the end of the Verse, the statement: ‌ ‌ to (Allah is Most-Forgiving, Very-Merciful) makes a pointed reference to the fact that these unlawful things are still unlawful as they already were, but only such a person has been given leave because of the state of compulsion he may be in. (This) that which I have mentioned to you of transgressions and the unlawful (is an abomination) engaging in them is an abomination and declaring them lawful is an act of disbelief.

**What the heedless soul and the carrion carry.**

By way of allusion He is saying that when this Adamic soul is killed by the sword of struggle in the path of discipline according to the Shariah-that is, when it has been subjugated by the religion and come to be commanded by the Shariah, made a servant and abased by the burden of obedience-the soul with this description is pure. But whenever a soul dies in the darkness of its own heedlessness such that it no longer perceives the work of the religion and exerts no effort in the limits set down by the Shariah, this soul is like the carrion whose body is defiled and nearness to which is forbidden. Hence this carrion is worse than that carrion, and its prohibition is greater.

4.text:
The question comes from people who want a rule rather than an opinion, and the answer is given as a general principle first. “They ask you, O Prophet, what is permissible for them to eat, Say” names the question and hands the reply to the one who speaks for God, so the ruling comes from revelation and not from custom. The principle itself is brief, “What is good and lawful”, which makes the clean things the rule and leaves the rest outside it. To that the verse brings in the case of the animals that hunt for their owners: “Also what is caught by your hunting animals and birds of prey which you have trained as instructed by Allah”, and training is the condition named, so a beast that brings down game for its master stands in the place of the master’s own hand. The permission is then stated in the plainest words, “So eat what they catch for you”, with one condition attached, “but mention the Name of Allah over it first”, which keeps the act of killing under the name of God even when teeth and claws did the work. The verse ends with the attitude that keeps the ruling in place, “And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning”, and the last phrase is a warning about time, since the account is close and nothing is forgotten. Hunting with a trained animal is therefore a trust rather than a simple permission, since the beast is a tool, the Name stands over the act, and the one who eats is answerable for what he ate and for how it was taken. The same care belongs to everything else in the verse, since the food that is good, the animal that is trained and the Name that is mentioned over the catch are all parts of one rule, which is that what a person takes into his body and what he does with his hands are both seen.

**The people who asked and the answer they were given.**

(They ask thee) O Muhammad; the people who so asked were Zayd Ibn Muhalhil al-Ta'i and 'Adiyy Ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, both fishermen (what is made lawful for them) of game. Some Companions had asked the Holy Prophet about the rule governing hunting with the help of a trained dog and falcon. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed (They ask thee (O Muhammad) what is made lawful for them. Say: good things are made lawful for you. And those beasts and birds of prey) . Gabriel, peace be upon him, went to see the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, but did not enter in on the Prophet even though he was granted permission to enter. When the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, commanded the killing of dogs, a group of people went to him and said:

**What is good and lawful to eat.**

(Say: good things) all the immolated ones (are made lawful for you. And those beasts and birds of prey which ye have trained as hounds are trained, ye teach them) to abstain from eating game (that which Allah taught you) as Allah has taught you; (so eat of that which they) the trained dogs (catch for you and mention Allah's name upon it) upon immolating your game; and it is also said: upon sending the trained dogs upon the game, (and observe your duty to Allah) fear Allah about eating the meat of carrion. Allah has permitted you to eat any food that is pure and also what is hunted by trained animals that have canines, such as dogs, cheetahs, or birds that have talons such as falcons. All those things which are considered clean and perfectly formed in the eyes of nature, and all those animals whose nature is compatible with human nature, are all legitimate and permissible for human consumption. Say ‘The good delicious things are made lawful for you; and the quarry of hunting creatures dogs wildcats or birds that catch food you have taught training them as hounds mukallibīn is a circumstantial qualifier derived from kallabtu al-kalba meaning ‘I released the hound against the quarry’ teaching them tu‘allimūnahunna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of mukallibīn ‘training them as hounds’ in other words ‘disciplining them’ of what God has taught you of the art of hunting; so eat what they have caught for you even if they have killed it as long as they have not eaten any of it.

**The animals trained to hunt for you.**

When the beast is trained, and it catches the game for its owner who mentioned Allah's Name when he sent the beast after the game, then this game is allowed according to the consensus of scholars, even if it was killed. (training them in the manner as directed to you by Allah,) as when the beast is sent, it goes after the game, and when it catches it, it keeps it until its owner arrives and does not catch it to eat it itself. The verse widens the table and the marriage law at once, and the day is named again as the moment the widening came. “Today all good, pure foods have been made lawful for you. Similarly, the food of the People of the Book is permissible for you and yours is permissible for them”, so the permission rests on what is clean in itself and not on the community that supplies it, and the exchange runs both ways, since the meat they slaughter may be eaten by the believers and the food of the believers may be offered to them. The same openness is then applied to marriage: “And permissible for you in marriage are chaste believing women as well as chaste women of those given the Scripture before you”, with chastity named as the quality that matters, and the phrase that follows sets the terms of the contract, “as long as you pay them their dowries in wedlock”. The honour of the union is guarded by the next phrase, “neither fornicating nor taking them as mistresses”, which rules out the secret arrangement that keeps the appearance of the union while losing its meaning. The verse then turns to the other side of the matter, since a permission is not an open door to treat faith lightly: “And whoever rejects the faith” is the choice that puts a person outside, and the consequence is given in full, “all their good deeds will be void in this life and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers”. The good they did is not described as evil; it is lost as a claim, because the faith it was built on has been let go. The permission to share a table and a marriage with the People of the Book is therefore held in place by the seriousness of the faith itself, and the one who keeps the permission without keeping the faith has taken the part that suits him and left the rest.

The verse has one subject, the preparation of the body and the heart for standing before God, and it sets out the conditions in the order in which a person meets them. “O believers! The next clauses deal with the state of the body, “And if you are in a state of full impurity, then take a full bath”, which is the greater washing, and then come the cases in which a person cannot reach water at all: “But if you are ill, on a journey, or have relieved yourselves, or have been intimate with your wives and cannot find water, then purify yourselves with clean earth by wiping your faces and hands”. The list is wide on purpose, so illness, travel and the ordinary calls of the body all have a way out, and the earth takes the place of water in the same movement of face and hands. The verse then answers the fear that these commands are a weight: “It is not Allah’s Will to burden you, but to purify you and complete His favour upon you”, so the washing is described as a means of cleaning and of a favour brought to its end, not as a load laid on the body. The last phrase names what all of this is meant to produce, “so perhaps you will be grateful”, and gratitude is put as the aim of the whole instruction. Read as one passage, the verse moves from the limbs to the water, from the water to the earth, and from the earth to the heart, which is the order the rest of the sūrah keeps when it speaks of what a believer owes to the One who gave him the gift of the prayer itself. Nothing in the list is arbitrary, since each part is named with the limit that belongs to it, and the concession for water and earth is placed beside the commands to show that the aim is the cleaning of the person and not the burdening of him.

The verse turns the reader back to what he has already received and already promised, and it does so in one long opening clause: “Remember Allah’s favour upon you and the covenant He made with you when you said, We hear and obey”. The favour is named first, because the reminder is meant to begin with a gift rather than with a demand, and the covenant comes next, the pledge that was spoken aloud by the people themselves. “We hear and obey” is quoted as their own sentence, kept in the form of hearing and following, so the promise is not a formality but the acceptance of a command before it is fully known. “And be mindful of Allah” then keeps the memory in place, since remembering a favour can slide into taking it for granted, and the mindfulness asked for here is the guard against that. The verse closes with the knowledge that makes the whole reminder serious: “Surely Allah knows best what is hidden in the heart”, so the covenant is weighed by what is inside a person and not only by what he said where others could hear him. A favour remembered, a promise kept and a heart laid open are the three movements of the verse, and the last of them explains why the first two cannot be left as words alone. The verse is a reminder rather than a new command, and that is why it asks for nothing more than attention to what has already been given and already promised, since a people who forget a favour will soon think that what they have came from themselves, and a people who forget a pledge will treat the promise as a word they once spoke in passing.

**The favour and the covenant that bound you.**

(Remember Allah's grace) recollect Allah's blessing (upon you) through faith (and His covenant) pledge (by which He bound you) with which He commanded you on the Day of the Covenant (when you said: We hear) Your words, O our Lord, (and we obey) Your command; (and keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in that which He commanded and prohibited you. The verse gives the community two duties that sit together, a firm stand and a true word. “O believers! Stand firm for Allah and bear true testimony” names both at once, since standing for God is not a posture of the body but the practice of saying what is true, and the testimony is meant to be given for God rather than for a side. The danger the verse guards against is named in the next phrase: “Do not let the hatred of a people lead you to injustice. Be just!” The warning is put in the middle of a community that had good reason to resent those who had wronged it, and the command is not to let that reason become a licence, so justice is owed to the people one hates as much as to the people one loves. “That is closer to righteousness” states the gain, and the word used makes the distance small on purpose: the just act is nearer to the fear of God than its opposite, and nearer is enough for a person to choose it. “And be mindful of Allah” then repeats the guard under which the whole instruction stands, and “Surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do” closes with the knowledge that reaches the act itself rather than the report of it. A stand taken for God, a testimony kept true, and a justice that survives hatred are one demand here, and the verse leaves the reader with the sense that none of the three is hidden from the One who asked for them.

**Standing firm for Allah and true testimony.**

(O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity) in justice, (and let not hatred of any people) the hatred of Shurayh Ibn Shurahbil (seduce you) drive you (that ye deal not justly) with the pilgrims of the clan of Bakr Ibn Wa'il. Stand out firmly for Allah as just witnesses; and let not the enmity and hatred of others make you avoid justice. It is recorded in the Two Sahihs that An-Nu'man bin Bashir said, "My father gave me a gift, but 'Amrah bint Rawahah, my mother, said that she would not agree to it unless he made Allah's Messenger as a witness to it. So, my father went to Allah's Messenger to ask him to be a witness to his giving me the gift. (I shall not be witness to injustice.) My father then returned and took back his gift. (Deal justly) with them, (that is nearer to your duty) justice is nearer to God-fearingness as far as the God-fearing are concerned.

**The hatred that must not lead to injustice.**

(and let not the enmity and hatred of others make you avoid justice.) Do not be carried away by your hatred for some people to avoid observing justice with them. Rather, be just with every one, whether a friend or an enemy. Let not hatred of a people namely the disbelievers cause you not to be just and to harm them on account of their enmity; be just towards both friend and foe that justice is nearer to God-fearing. The hatred for a people should not make you leave justice: justice is a requirement with a friend, as well as with an enemy, so be just with both.

**Justice and what is nearer to righteousness.**

(Be just: that is nearer to Taqwa) this is better than if you abandon justice in this case. Although Allah said that observing justice is 'nearer to Taqwa', there is not any other course of action to take, therefore 'nearer' here means 'is'. This is the reason why, by placing 'al-qist' (justice) first in the verse of the Surah al-Nisa', it was said: ... be upholders of justice, witnesses for Allah ...) and, by placing 'lillah' (for Allah) first in the verse of Surah al-Ma'idah, it was said: ... be steadfast for Allah as witnesses for justice) - though, both these modes serve the same purpose end-wise. Therefore, the words which follow this sentence in Surah Al-Nisa' ‌ that is, 'even though against yourselves or the parents, and the kinsfolk ...' After the sentence of Surah al-Ma'idah cited above, the words which follow in this verse are: ‌ that is, And malice against a people should not bid you to not doing justice ...' So, the essential message of this verse of Surah al-Nisa' is:

The verse closes on the power behind the sending: “And Allah is Most Capable of everything”, able to send the messengers and able to send the last of them, and able to hold every one of his addressees to what has now been made clear.

Rather, He is the Final Messenger who came after a long time passed between him and 'Isa, son of Maryam peace be upon them. O People of the Scripture there has verily come to you Our Messenger Muhammad making clear to you the laws of religion after an interval between the messengers for there was no messenger between him and Jesus an interval of 569 years; lest you should say if you are punished ‘There has not come to us any bearer of good tidings min bashīr the min is extra nor any warner’. When, by addressing the people of the Book in this verse, it was said that Our Messenger, Muhammad al-Mustafa has come after a long gap,' there emerges a subtle hint towards the need that people who have been honoured with his presence among them should consider this as a matchless blessing and a supreme asset because the line of prophets had remained suspended since a long time and it has been opened for them once again. O People of the Scripture, Jews and Christians, My messenger Muhammad ﷺ has come to you after a period when there were no messengers and when there was a real need for his mission, so that you do not say as an excuse, ‘No messenger came to us bringing good news of Allah’s reward nor any warning of His punishment’. It is the way of God that He, on His behalf, raises certain individuals who acquaint the people with the realities of life; warn them of hell and give them the good news of paradise. It is only by supporting these ‘warners’ and ‘bringers of good news’ and cooperating with them that man finds God, and not in any other way.

**The Messenger, the messengers and what follows.**

There is no contradiction here if we consider the fact that those who said that this period was six hundred years were talking about solar years, while the second refers to lunar years, since there is a difference of about three years between every one hundred lunar and solar years. (lest you say, "There came unto us no bringer of glad tidings and no warner.") meaning, so that you, who changed the true religion, do not make it an excuse and say, "No Messenger came to us bringing glad tidings and warning against evil. This, then, becomes a widely witnessed and authentically verified proof that he was a Prophet and Messenger of Allah and that his prophetic teachings were the most effective and the most surpassing among those coming from all past prophets. Imagine the mission of a physician who treats a hopeless patient and does it at a place which lacks medical instruments, and medicines too, yet he succeeds in his effort to treat the patient to the limit that this patient, not simply that he rises from his death-bed to be-come a healthy person, but that he goes way ahead and himself turns into an expert physician and healer as well - if so, who can doubt the perfection of the master healer! (Now hath a messenger) Muhammad ﷺ (of cheer) announcing Paradise (and a warner) against hell (come unto you. Allah is Able to do all things): whether it be sending messengers, rewarding those who follow the messengers or punishing those who do not follow the messengers.

**The messengers and the messenger.**

The religion was distorted and changed for the people of the earth until Allah sent Muhammad , and Allah, thus, guided the creatures and took them away from the darkness to the light and placed them on a clear path and a glorious Law. As for the three messengers mentioned in Surah Ya Sin , they were messengers sent by Sayyidna Isa who have been' called messengers (bearers of a message) in the literal sense. About the appearance of Khalid ibn Sinan al- Arabi during this gap as reported by some chroniclers, Tafsir Ruh al-Ma'ani says with reference to Shihab that his being a prophet is correct, but the period in which he came was earlier than Sayyidna Isa, not after him. (Now hath Our messenger) Muhammad ﷺ (come unto you to make things plain) that with which you have been commanded and that which you have been prohibited (after an interval) of cessation (of the messengers, lest ye should say) so that you will not say on the Day of Judgement:

20.text:
The verse takes the reader back to an older community and to a leader speaking with his people: “And remember when Moses said to his people, O my people, Remember Allah”. The two sentences of the address are joined, so the remembering asked of them is the very remembering that Moses himself demonstrates: “s favours upon you when He raised prophets from among you”. Prophets were raised among them, not strangers sent from another people, and their leader tells them to count these as gifts. The favours are then given a second form: “made you sovereign”, a kingship granted to them out of mercy, for the period of their Prophet and afterwards they held the promise of the land and a rule that no other people of their time had been given. The last phrase sums the whole gift: “and gave you what He had never given anyone in the world”, a favour set apart for this people, a book, a prophet, and a dominion promised to them by the words of their father Israel. The verse does not stop at the enumeration of the gifts, and it does not leave them as a boast for the people who received them either, since Moses is made to mention them as the ground of an obedience still to come: a people reminded of so much is a people expected to hold to the covenant that came with it, and the following verses of the passage carry this reminder forward to the command that was laid on them to enter the promised land, a command they met first with hesitation and then with refusal, which is why the reminder of the favour is placed so close to the account of their failure to act on it.

**The people and the belief.**

Allah then sent down the revelation to the Final Prophet and Messenger, Muhammad, the son of 'Abdullah, from the offspring of Isma'il, the son of Ibrahim, peace be upon them. (which Allah has assigned to you) meaning, which Allah has promised to you by the words of your father Isra'il, that it is the inheritance of those among you who believe. **The people and the Israelites.**

(and gave you what He had not given to any other among the nations (Al-'Alamin).) means, during your time, as we stated. The hint given here is that the people of Bani' Isra'il who were the oppressed slaves of the Pharaoh and his people for many ages saw how Allah Ta ala destroyed their enemies and how they themselves were made masters and kings. Remember, O Messenger, when Moses said to his people, the Israelites, ‘O People, remember, with your hearts and tongues, Allah’s favour to you when He made prophets amongst you calling you to guidance, made you kings in control of your affairs after you were subjugated slaves, and gave you such favours that He had not given to any other people in your time’. (And (remember) when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Remember Allah's favour) Allah's grace (unto you, how He placed among you) from you (Prophets, and He made you Kings) while you were slaves of Pharaoh before, (and gave you that (which) He gave not to any (other) of creatures) of your time in the wilderness: quails and honey.

**The Prophet and the Jihad.**

(And (remember) when Musa said to his people: "O my people! Remember the favor of Allah to you, when He made Prophets among you,) for whenever a Prophet died, another rose among them, from the time of their father Ibrahim and thereafter. **What the theft carries.**

(So Ifruq us from the rebellious people!) Al-'Awfi reported that Ibn 'Abbas said, "Meaning, judge between us and them." 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported similarly from him. Yuwsha' said, 'Some of you have committed theft from the booty.' So he summoned the twelve leaders of the twelve tribes and took the pledge from them. Then, the hand of one of them became stuck to the hand of Yuwsha' and Yuwsha' said, 'You committed the theft, so bring it forth.' So, that man brought a cow's head made of gold with two eyes made of precious stones and a set of teeth made of pearls. (He made prophets from among you) which carries the sense that the whole people were not prophets, and this is the truth as prophets are only a few while the large body of people follows them. 21.text:
The verse continues the address of Moses to his people, and it opens with the tenderness the earlier words carried: “O my people”. He is speaking to his own kin, and the command he lays before them is the gift he wants them to take: “Enter the Holy Land which Allah has destined for you to enter”. The land is named as holy, purified, the country of Damascus and Palestine and the land around Bayt al-Maqdis, the land Allah had promised the Children of Israel by the words of their father Israel and had commanded them to enter. The command is given as a destiny already prepared and not as a conquest to be won, so the people are asked to walk into what has been made ready for them rather than to trust the measure of their own strength. The verse then warns against the one thing that could keep them out: “And do not turn back or else you will become losers”. Turning back here is retreating from the fight, going back on the heels after the command has been given, and the loss is named as the fruit of it, a loss in this world and a loss in the world to come, since a people who turn away from what Allah has destined for them lose the gift and the standing that came with it at once. The warning shows where the danger lay: the task was entering, and the only way to fail at it was to refuse the entry, so the verse sets the land in front of the people and the loss behind them and leaves the choice where it belongs.

**The people and the Messenger.**

Allah states that His servant, Messenger, to whom He spoke directly, Musa, the son of 'Imran, reminded his people that among the favors Allah granted them, is that He will give them all of the good of this life and the Hereafter, if they remain on the righteous and straight path. (And (remember) when Musa said to his people: "O my people! Remember the favor of Allah to you, when He made Prophets among you,) for whenever a Prophet died, another rose among them, from the time of their father Ibrahim and thereafter. Allah states next that Musa encouraged the Children of Israel to perform Jihad and enter Bayt al-Maqdis, which was under their control during the time of their father Ya'qub. Musa, Allah's Messenger, ordered the Children of Israel to enter Bayt al-Maqdis and fight their enemy, and he promised them victory and triumph over the mighty people if they did so. (which Allah has assigned to you) meaning, which Allah has promised to you by the words of your father Isra'il, that it is the inheritance of those among you who believe. When the Children of Israel declined to obey Allah and follow His Messenger Musa, two righteous men among them, on whom Allah had bestowed a great bounty and who were afraid of Allah and His punishment, encouraged them to go forward. Therefore, they said, if you rely on and trust in Allah, follow His command and obey His Messenger, then Allah will give you victory over your enemies and will give you triumph and dominance over them. When Musa supplicated against the Jews for refusing to fight in Jihad, Allah forbade them from entering the land for forty years. Next, Allah commanded Yuwsha' to order the Children of Israel to enter Bayt al-Maqdis from its gate while bowing and saying Hittah, meaning, 'remove our sins.' Yet, they changed what they were commanded and entered it while dragging themselves on their behinds and saying, 'Habbah (a seed) in Sha'rah (a hair). They also witnessed the torment and punishment of drowning with which Allah punished their enemy Fir'awn and his soldiers, so that their eyes were pleased and comforted. The saying of Sayyidna Musa in the first verse was his introductory remark to the Divine command which appears in the following verse in the words: ‌ (0 my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has destined for you ...). Sayyidna Ka'b al-Ahbar has said that he has seen in the Book of Allah (perhaps, the Torah) that the country of Syria is a special treasure of Allah on this entire earth and there are in it Allah's very special and very dear servants. According to some narrations, on a day when Sayyidna Ibrahim climbed a mountain in Lebanon, Allah Ta ala said: 0 Ibrahim, look from here and as far as you will see, that land We have made the Holy Land. Moses said, ‘O People, enter the land that has been purified – Bayt al-Maqdis and the surrounding area – which Allah has promised that you will enter, and fight the disbelievers in it. (O my people! Go into the holy land) the purified Damascus, Palestine and parts of Jordan (which Allah hath ordained for you) which Allah has gifted to you and made it a bequest of your father Abraham.

**The people and the world.**

In it are a people of great strength, and we shall never enter it, till they leave it; when they leave, then we will enter. Their excuse was this, in this very town you commanded us to enter and fight its people, there is a mighty, strong, vicious people who have tremendous physique and physical ability. Therefore, they said, we are incapable of entering this city as long as they are still in it, but if they leave it, we will enter it. O my people enter the Holy the purified Land which God has ordained for you which He commanded you to enter and this is Syria al-shām and do not turn back in flight do not retreat in fear of the enemy or you will end up as losers’ in your efforts. Still others point out to the city of Ariha which was located between the Jordan river and Baytul-Maqdis and was reported to be one of the oldest cities of the world. Just as God requires of a community that it should represent His religion, similarly He also wants the community representing His religion to enjoy honours and high position in this world, so that it should be demonstrated to the people that in the new world coming into existence after Doomsday, prominence and distinction will be conferred only upon the ‘People of the Truth’.

**The land and the They.**

They declined, rebelled and defied his order and were punished for forty years by being lost, wandering in the land uncertain of where they should go. "They wandered in the land for forty years, during which Musa and Harun died, as well as everyone above forty years of age. According to later narrations, the whole country of Syria is the Holy Land - it is just that some narrators have described a certain part of the country of Syria while some others have identified the whole of it.

22.text:
The people answer their prophet, and the answer begins with the name they had always used for him: “They replied, O Moses”. What they report is a fact about the land, “There is an enormously powerful people there”, the giants of the remnant of the people of Aad, mighty in body and certain to fight, so the report itself is not false, but it is offered as a reason for refusing to move. From that report they draw their own conclusion: “so we will never be able to enter it until they leave”. The task is left hanging on the departure of the inhabitants, as though the promise of Allah could only come true when the enemy chose to walk away. The last two phrases put the whole matter into the enemy's hands: “If they do, then we will enter”. Everything was made conditional on what those inside the city would do, and nothing was left to the power that had drowned the army of the tyrant in the sea and split the water to bring this people out of it. The verse thus shows what the report of a strong enemy does in a heart that has begun to count its own strength: the promise is not denied outright, it is postponed onto a condition the people themselves will never fulfil, and the answer ends with the very refusal the earlier verse had warned them against, made polite by being put as a plan.

**The people and the command.**

Allah states that His servant, Messenger, to whom He spoke directly, Musa, the son of 'Imran, reminded his people that among the favors Allah granted them, is that He will give them all of the good of this life and the Hereafter, if they remain on the righteous and straight path. Musa, Allah's Messenger, ordered the Children of Israel to enter Bayt al-Maqdis and fight their enemy, and he promised them victory and triumph over the mighty people if they did so. Therefore, they said, we are incapable of entering this city as long as they are still in it, but if they leave it, we will enter it. Therefore, they said, if you rely on and trust in Allah, follow His command and obey His Messenger, then Allah will give you victory over your enemies and will give you triumph and dominance over them. (They said, "O Musa! We shall never enter it as long as they are there. So go, you and your Lord, and fight you two, we are sitting right here.") Next, Allah commanded Yuwsha' to order the Children of Israel to enter Bayt al-Maqdis from its gate while bowing and saying Hittah, meaning, 'remove our sins.' Yet, they changed what they were commanded and entered it while dragging themselves on their behinds and saying, 'Habbah (a seed) in Sha'rah (a hair). All this did not happen too long ago, yet they refused to perform Jihad against people who had less than a tenth of the power and strength than the people of Egypt had. They said ‘O Moses there are giants in it those remaining of the people of ‘Ād who were very tall and mighty; we will never enter it until they depart from it; if they depart from it then we will enter’ it. (They said, 0 Musa ...), it will be recalled that, in the verse previous to it , Allah Ta ala had commanded the Bani Isra'il through Sayyidna Musa that they should wage a Jihad against the Amalkites and conquer Syria given along with it was the good news that the land of Syria has been destined for them, therefore, their victory is certain. Instead of doing that, they said: 0 Musa, there is a nation of tyrants over there, and we shall never go in there until they get out of it. Finally, they agreed upon the proposal that they should be allowed to go free so that they could return to their people and become walking eye witnesses of the great power and grandeur of the Amalkites against which they would never dare to think of marching. Since they are the remnants of the people of Ad whose awesome height and size has been mentioned by the Holy Qur'an itself, so, their huge size and unusual strength were proverbial. (They said: O Moses! Lo! a giant people) assassins ((dwell) therein, and lo! we go not in) this land of assassins (till they go forth from thence. When they go forth, then we will enter (not till then).

**What the people carries.**

(And (remember) when Musa said to his people: "O my people! Remember the favor of Allah to you, when He made Prophets among you,) for whenever a Prophet died, another rose among them, from the time of their father Ibrahim and thereafter. Then, the hand of one of them became stuck to the hand of Yuwsha' and Yuwsha' said, 'You committed the theft, so bring it forth.' So, that man brought a cow's head made of gold with two eyes made of precious stones and a set of teeth made of pearls. His people said to him, ‘O Moses, in the Holy Land there is a powerful and mighty people and this is preventing us from entering it. Just as God requires of a community that it should represent His religion, similarly He also wants the community representing His religion to enjoy honours and high position in this world, so that it should be demonstrated to the people that in the new world coming into existence after Doomsday, prominence and distinction will be conferred only upon the ‘People of the Truth’. It has to prove that it has full faith in God under all circumstances and bows to His will and pleasure even if that tries their patience to the very limits.

**What the final carries.**

Enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and turn not back; for then you will be returned as losers. There were many Prophets among the Children of Israel calling to Allah and warning against His torment, until 'Isa was sent as the final Prophet from the Children of Israel. Allah then sent down the revelation to the Final Prophet and Messenger, Muhammad, the son of 'Abdullah, from the offspring of Isma'il, the son of Ibrahim, peace be upon them.

23.text:
Two men stand out from the rest of the people and speak: “Two God-fearing men, who had been blessed by Allah, said”. They are men who feared the command of Allah more than the enemy in front of them, Joshua and Caleb, two of the upright, and they are described as blessed because the fear in their hearts was itself a gift and not a quality they had made for themselves. Their advice is direct: “Surprise them through the gate”. Do not stand in the open and count the enemy; enter on them at the gate of the town, and the entry will be yours. Then comes the promise: “If you do, you will certainly prevail”, a victory made certain by the command of Allah and not by the number of those who fight. The two men close with the ground of the promise: “Put your trust in Allah if you are truly believers”. They spoke with assurance because they trusted, and the people around them who said they believed are asked to bring out of that belief what it must produce, a reliance on Allah that walks through the gate instead of calculating what waits on the other side of it. The verse therefore sets two hearts beside a whole crowd and shows that the difference between them was not the measure of the enemy but the measure of trust. The men who spoke were not stronger than those who stayed silent, and nothing in the passage suggests that they had a plan the others lacked; what they had was the certainty that the promise of Allah would be kept by Allah himself, and that certainty is the whole content of their advice.

**The Messenger and the blessing.**

Allah states that His servant, Messenger, to whom He spoke directly, Musa, the son of 'Imran, reminded his people that among the favors Allah granted them, is that He will give them all of the good of this life and the Hereafter, if they remain on the righteous and straight path. (And (remember) when Musa said to his people: "O my people! Remember the favor of Allah to you, when He made Prophets among you,) for whenever a Prophet died, another rose among them, from the time of their father Ibrahim and thereafter. (And indeed We gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, and the understanding of the Scripture and its laws, and the Prophethood; and provided them with good things, and preferred them above the nations (Al-'Alamin).)[45:16] Allah said,. (which Allah has assigned to you) meaning, which Allah has promised to you by the words of your father Isra'il, that it is the inheritance of those among you who believe. When the Children of Israel declined to obey Allah and follow His Messenger Musa, two righteous men among them, on whom Allah had bestowed a great bounty and who were afraid of Allah and His punishment, encouraged them to go forward. Therefore, they said, if you rely on and trust in Allah, follow His command and obey His Messenger, then Allah will give you victory over your enemies and will give you triumph and dominance over them. In the Book of Al-Maghazi and At-Tafsir, Al-Bukhari recorded that 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud said, "On the day of Badr, Al-Miqdad said, 'O Messenger of Allah! (O my Lord! I have power only over myself and my brother') meaning, only I and my brother Harun among them will obey, implement Allah's command and accept the call,. During this time, tremendous miracles occurred, such as the clouds that shaded them and the manna and quails Allah sent down for them. Next, Allah commanded Yuwsha' to order the Children of Israel to enter Bayt al-Maqdis from its gate while bowing and saying Hittah, meaning, 'remove our sins.' Yet, they changed what they were commanded and entered it while dragging themselves on their behinds and saying, 'Habbah (a seed) in Sha'rah (a hair). May Allah curse their faces that were transformed to the shape of swine and apes, and may Allah's curse accompany them to the raging Fire. : that is, 'Allah had blessed them.' The hint given here is that whoever has any excellence in him anywhere, that is nothing but the blessing and favour of Allah Ta ala - otherwise, these twelve chiefs were all blessed with similar outward gifts of hands, feet, eyes and ears with reason and sense on the inside, along with the fortunate company of Sayyidna Musa They had all the strengths on their side, yet they all slipped except these two who stood firm on their commitment. The standard rule of conduct we learn from here is that a person whom Allah Ta ala has blessed with reason, intelligence and smartness should not wax proud over these personal strengths while conducting the business of his life. Two men from the companions of Moses who feared Allah and were afraid of His punishment, whom Allah had blessed by enabling them to obey Him, urged their people to fulfil the instruction of Moses and said, ‘Enter the gate of the city against the tyrants. Once you go through the gate you will – by Allah’s permission – defeat them, as Allah’s custom is to give victory after the means of having faith and making preparation are adopted. (Then spoke two of those who feared) two men who feared the assassins (unto whom Allah had been gracious) by bestowing upon them the certainty of inspiration; these two men were Joshua ben Nun and Caleb ben Jephunneh: (Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) that you will be victorious (if ye are indeed believers) it is also said that the two men who said this are two men from the assassins who feared Moses and with whom Allah was gracious by bestowing upon them belief in Allah's divine Oneness.

**The them and the they.**

There said to them two men of those who feared contravening God’s command and these were Joshua and Caleb — who were from among the leaders that Moses dispatched to bring back news of those giants — to whom God had been gracious by making them virtuous for they concealed what they had discovered about the giants telling only Moses unlike the other leaders who divulged the news and so the people became cowardly. ‘Enter against them by the gate! the gate of the town and have no fear of them for they are bodies without hearts.

**The they and the will.**

Therefore, they said, we are incapable of entering this city as long as they are still in it, but if they leave it, we will enter it. For if you enter by it you will be victorious the two Joshua and Caleb said this because they were certain of God’s assistance and the fulfilment of His promise. As for the decisive statement of these elders that once they reach the city gate, they will overcome and the enemy will run away defeated, it could have been based on a close assessment of the Amalkites, that they were, no doubt, unusually huge in built and strength, but were also weak at heart as a result of which, once they hear about the surprise attack, they would be unable to stay there.-And it is also possible that their total faith in the Divine decree which they had heard from Sayyidna Musa as a glad tiding was the basis on which they said so.

24.text:
The people answer again, and this time the answer is a flat refusal dressed as a condition: “Yet they said, O Moses”. Their words mix a report with their own decision: “Still we will never enter as long as they remain there, So go”. They made the presence of the enemy the end of the matter and the entry impossible while a single one of them was inside, so the promise of Allah was set aside by the plain arithmetic of strength. What follows is a taunt, and it is the ugliest sentence a people ever addressed to their prophet: “both you and your Lord, and fight”. They set the Prophet and his Lord on one side and themselves on the other, as though the work of the covenant belonged to Moses and to Allah while the people kept to their seats. The last phrase closes the door: “we are staying right here”. Their rebellion is not excused by the weakness they claimed, since the sitting still was their own choice and not merely their fear. The verse therefore places against the trust of the two men a refusal that asks its prophet to fight alongside his Lord while the people watch, and the mercy that had brought them out of the sea is answered by a demand that the sea be crossed for them again.
