Musa, Allah's Messenger, ordered the Children of Israel to enter Bayt al-Maqdis and fight their enemy, and he promised them victory and triumph over the mighty people if they did so. (which Allah has assigned to you) meaning, which Allah has promised to you by the words of your father Isra'il, that it is the inheritance of those among you who believe. In the Book of Al-Maghazi and At-Tafsir, Al-Bukhari recorded that 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud said, "On the day of Badr, Al-Miqdad said, 'O Messenger of Allah! When Musa supplicated against the Jews for refusing to fight in Jihad, Allah forbade them from entering the land for forty years. Next, Allah commanded Yuwsha' to order the Children of Israel to enter Bayt al-Maqdis from its gate while bowing and saying Hittah, meaning, 'remove our sins.' Yet, they changed what they were commanded and entered it while dragging themselves on their behinds and saying, 'Habbah (a seed) in Sha'rah (a hair). When Yuwsha' was reminded that the day was Friday and the sun was about to set, while they were still attacking Bayt al-Maqdis, he feared that the Sabbath might begin. Then, a Sahabi, Sayyidna Miqdad ibn al-Aswad stepped forward and said: 'Ya Rasul Allah , we swear by Allah we shall never say what was said to Sayyidna Musa by his people, that is ‌ (So go, you and your Lord, and fight. As for us, we are sitting right here).

**What the people carries.**

(and gave you what He had not given to any other among the nations (Al-'Alamin).) means, during your time, as we stated. They declined, rebelled and defied his order and were punished for forty years by being lost, wandering in the land uncertain of where they should go. Their excuse was this, in this very town you commanded us to enter and fight its people, there is a mighty, strong, vicious people who have tremendous physique and physical ability. It was also said that the Ayah reads in a way that means that these men were respected and honored by their people. All this did not happen too long ago, yet they refused to perform Jihad against people who had less than a tenth of the power and strength than the people of Egypt had.

25.text:
The prophet of the people turns from them to his Lord, and the plea begins with the name of the One he calls on: “Moses pleaded, My Lord”. He states what he has and what he does not: “I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother”. The words are not a complaint against Allah but a plain account of the ground he stands on, since the people who had answered him with their taunt about his Lord and their refusal to move were not in his hand to lead. What he asks for is a separation: “So set us apart from the rebellious people”. The word is one that divides one thing from another, and the request is that he and his brother Aaron be placed on the side of obedience while the people who refused the command remain where their refusal put them. The verse therefore shows a prophet at the end of his patience, and it leaves the ordering of the nation to Allah alone, since the one who had spoken with his Lord face to face still had no power over the hearts of those standing beside him.

**What the people carries.**

Their excuse was this, in this very town you commanded us to enter and fight its people, there is a mighty, strong, vicious people who have tremendous physique and physical ability. (O my Lord! I have power only over myself and my brother') meaning, only I and my brother Harun among them will obey, implement Allah's command and accept the call,. Yuwsha' said, 'Some of you have committed theft from the booty.' So he summoned the twelve leaders of the twelve tribes and took the pledge from them. The prayer of Sayyidna Musa ; ‌ "0 My Lord, I have no control except over myself" should be seen in the perspective of the events in the life of the people of Bani Isra'il, the favours of Allah bestowed upon them and the conduct of their prophet, Sayyidna Musa in their case. Their next generation survived and it was this generation which, after having been delivered from this forty year detention, entered Baytul-Maqdis; or, there were some people from the earlier generation who were still surviving.

**The over and the from.**

(So Ifruq us from the rebellious people!) Al-'Awfi reported that Ibn 'Abbas said, "Meaning, judge between us and them." 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported similarly from him. And finally, how was the wealth, over which the Pharaoh waxed proud by saying: ‌ ‌ ‌ (Is it not that this land of Egypt is for me and these are rivers which flow from beneath me?) given out by Allah Ta ala, the entire country and the entire wealth, without any fighting or killing, to the Bani Isra'il. So, being in pain and anger, he mentioned only those he was certain would stand firm on truth - 'I have no control except over myself and my brother.'. (I have control of none but myself and my brother, so distinguish between us) judge between us (and the wrong-doing folk) the contravening folk.

**The people in these verses.**

He Moses thereupon said ‘My Lord I control none but myself and my brother and I control no one else to be able to force them to obedience. Let the greatest possible reformer in the world stop for a while, cross his hand over his heart and think what effect such low attitudes demonstrated by the people he was working for would have produced on him. And since Allah Ta ala is the Most Merciful of all those merciful, it is possible that these once disobedient people from the Bani Isra'il, after having witnessed the happenings around them, may have repented from their sins and may be it was in return for their act of repentance that they were being blessed with these rewards. God then decided that for forty years (1440 B.C. to 1400 B.C.) they would wander in the desert, by which time all those who were of the age of twenty years or more would have died and during this period a new generation living under new conditions would have grown up.

26.text:
The answer comes from Allah, and it is a judgment on the people who had refused: “Allah replied, Then this land is forbidden to them for forty years”. The land they had been commanded to enter is closed to them, not for a night or a month but for forty years, and the sentence is matched to the refusal, since they would not enter while the powerful people were inside it, and now they are kept out while the gift waits for another generation. The punishment is given its own shape in the next phrase: “during which they will wander through the land”. They go on moving without arriving, the whole generation wandering in the desert of Tih, and the wandering itself was a mercy as well as a penalty, since it kept them alive and kept the promise standing while the generation that had refused it died away. The verse then binds the prophet's own heart: “So do not grieve for the rebellious people”. Grief over their punishment must not become a complaint against the decree, so the prophet is told to hold his sorrow away from a people who chose what came to them. The passage ends on that tenderness: the judge is Allah, the decree is just, and the messenger is spared the sorrow of carrying a loss that belongs to those who made it. The forty years are also the measure of a generation, since the people who had refused the entry would not see it, and the children who grew up in the wandering would be the ones to cross the river and take what their fathers had turned away from. Moses and Aaron themselves died in the wilderness, and that death was a mercy for them and a separation from a people whose company had become a burden, so the closing words of the verse reach even the prophet's own grief and set it aside. The land did not go to the generation that refused it, and the promise did not lapse either, since the children who entered it were the answer to the oath that had been sworn at the beginning.

**The land that was forbidden.**

He God exalted be He said to him ‘Then it the Holy Land shall be forbidden them to enter for forty years; they shall wander lost bewildered in the land — according to Ibn ‘Abbās this land was about nine parasangs sc. 30 miles; so do not grieve for the wicked folk’. (For this the land will surely be forbidden them) i.e. to enter it, after you called them wrong-doing folk (for forty years that they will wander in the earth, bewildered) they will be bewildered in the wilderness, confined in an area of seven parasangs, unable to get out of it or be guided to the right way. Allah said to His Prophet Moses ﷺ, ‘Allah has forbidden entry into the Holy Land for the Israelites for a period of forty years, in which they will wander on earth aimlessly without direction. God then decided that for forty years (1440 B.C. to 1400 B.C.) they would wander in the desert, by which time all those who were of the age of twenty years or more would have died and during this period a new generation living under new conditions would have grown up.

**The forty years and the wandering.**

In this wilderness of Tih, Sayyidna Musa and Harun were with their people for whom this wilderness was nothing but detention and punishment, while, for these two blessed souls, it was the fountain head of Divine blessings. Thus, Allah Ta ala detained a whole people whose total number, according to the statement of Sayyidna Muqatil was six hundred thousand, restricting them within this small open ground in a manner that they kept struggling for full forty years to somehow get out of this open land area and return back to Egypt, or go forward and reach Baytul-Maqdis. In the forty years spent in the desert, all the people of advanced age died. And they would travel all day with the same result until they all perished except those under twenty years of age. Moses and Aaron died in the wilderness and this was a mercy for them and a chastisement for those others. Allah states that His servant, Messenger, to whom He spoke directly, Musa, the son of 'Imran, reminded his people that among the favors Allah granted them, is that He will give them all of the good of this life and the Hereafter, if they remain on the righteous and straight path. Hanbal reported in his Musnad the following hadīth ‘The sun was never detained for any human except for Joshua during those days in which he marched towards the Holy House of Bayt al-Maqdis’. This meant that they were more afraid of human beings than of God.

**The Children of Israel and the land.**

Therefore, they said, we are incapable of entering this city as long as they are still in it, but if they leave it, we will enter it. God informed the Children of Israel that the tyrant people had come to the end of their epoch, that they should enter that country and that with the help of God they would overcome the tyrant people after some negligible resistence. This is why this period of forty years during which the Bani Isra'il were condemned was still full of many silver linings. The Children of Israel had told Moses that if they invaded that country (of the Amalekites) they themselves would be defeated and their children would be treated as so much loot. Compare this to the better response the Companions gave to the Messenger of Allah during the battle of Badr, when he asked for their advice about fighting the Quraysh army that came to protect the caravan led by Abu Sufyan. (which Allah has assigned to you) meaning, which Allah has promised to you by the words of your father Isra'il, that it is the inheritance of those among you who believe.

**The grief and the punishment.**

(So grieve not over) do not be saddened about (the wrong-doing folk). Do not grieve, O Moses, over those who do not follow Allah, because the punishment they receive is because of their sins’. The substance of this prayer, according to an explanation given by Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Abbas was that 'the punishment these people deserved should be given to them; and whatever we are found to be deserving of should be awarded to us.'. So he sallied forth with those that remained by his side and he fought against them; it was a Friday and the sun stopped for him for an hour until he had finished with fighting them. It is reported that they would travel throughout the night earnestly but in the morning would find themselves back where they had started. According to authentic narrations, it was during this period of forty years that Sayyidna Harun died.

27.text:
The address turns from the wandering generation to a story that is to be told with care: “Relate to them in truth, O Prophet, the story of Adam’s two sons”. The two are Abel and Cain, and what is told of them is put in its plain form: “how each offered a sacrifice: Abel’s offering was accepted while Cain’s was not”. Both brought an offering, so the story is not about one man who worships and another who does not, but about two brothers whose worship was weighed and whose hearts were shown by what was received. The accepted offering belonged to the one who brought the best of his flock out of a heart of obedience, and the rejected one to the man who brought what he did not value, so the story shows that acceptance is not owed to a name or to a birth. When the rejection came, Cain did not turn and examine himself: “So Cain threatened, I will kill you”. The threat is the answer pride gives when it is told a truth it cannot meet, and the brother's reply is as calm as the first verses of the passage were fiery: “His brother replied, Allah only accepts the offering of the sincerely devout”. The criterion given is the heart that is mindful of Allah, in word and deed and offering alike, and the verse leaves the story resting on that criterion, since the killing that follows belongs to a heart that heard it and refused it.

**The truth and the sacrifice.**

Allah describes the evil end and consequence of transgression, envy and injustice in the story of the two sons of Adam, Habil and Qabil. (And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth;) meaning, tell these envious, unjust people, the brothers of swine and apes from the Jews and their likes among mankind, the story of the two sons of Adam, Habil and Qabil, as many scholars among the Salaf and later generations said. Several scholars among the Salaf and the later generations said that Allah allowed Adam to marry his daughters to his sons because of the necessity of such action. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said – that during the time of Adam – "The woman was not allowed in marriage for her male twin, but Adam was commanded to marry her to any of her other brothers. What does 'kill' mean?' He said, 'He will no longer eat, drink or move.' She said, 'And that is death?' He said, 'Yes it is.' So she started to weep until Adam came to her while she was weeping and said, 'What is the matter with you?' She did not answer him. And recite O Muhammad to them your people the story the tale of the two sons of Adam Abel and Cain truthfully bi’l-haqq is semantically connected to utlu ‘recite’ how they each offered a sacrifice to God which in Abel’s case was a ram and in Cain’s some green crops and it was accepted from one of them namely from Abel when a fire came down from the heaven and consumed his offering and not accepted from the other that is from Cain and so he became furious and kept secret his envy until Adam left on pilgrimage. In these verses, Allah Ta a1a has instructed the Holy Prophet that he should relate the story of the two sons of Adam truthfully to the people of the Book, or to the whole Ummah. (ibniy Adama: the two sons of Adam) appearing in the first verse , it can be said that, for that matter, every human being, man and woman, is from the progeny of Adam and everyone can be identified as being from among the children of Adam. But, according to the judgment of the majority of authentic scholars of Tafsir, the expression: at this place means the two real sons of Sayyidna Adam that is, Habil and Qabil. After this introduction, the event relating to these two sons of Adam was put in the following words by the Holy Qur'an: ‌ ‌ ‌ that is, both of them offered their sacrifices for Allah Ta ala, but it was accepted from one of them and was not accepted from the other. So, Allah Jalla Sha'nuhu, in terms of the need of the time, had promulgated a special provision in the religious law given to Sayyidna Adam that, as for a boy and girl born out of one pregnancy, they shall be regarded as real brothers and sisters among themselves and marriage between them shall be considered forbidden. The reason is that Sayyidna Adam was certain that the sacrifice to be accepted will be the sacrifice of the one who has the right to marry her, that is, the sacrifice of Habil. Relate with the truth O Messenger, to these Jews who are jealous and who do wrong, the incident of the two sons of Adam, Cain and Abel, When they both offered a sacrifice to gain closeness to Allah, Allah accepted the sacrifice offered by Abel because he was mindful of Him and did not accept the offering of Cain because he was not mindful of Allah. (But recite unto them) O Muhammad (with truth) with the Qur'an (the tale of the two sons of Adam, how they offered each a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the one) Abel (of them and it was not accepted from the other) Cain.

**The sacrifice and the offering.**

One of them fought against the other and killed him out of envy and transgression, because of the bounty that Allah gave his brother and because the sacrifice that he sincerely offered to Allah was accepted. So he said, 'You and your daughters will inherit the practice of weeping, while I and my sons are free of it.'" Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it. He said to him ‘I will surely slay you’ and the other said ‘Why?’ to which the first replied ‘Because only your offering was accepted’. In those days, an open sign of a sacrifice being accepted was that a fire would come from the sky and eat up the sacrifice; and the sacrifice which was not eaten up by the fire was the sign of its remaining unacceptable. (Allah accepts only from the God-fearing) that is, if you had been God-fearing, practicing Taqwa and piety, your sacrifice too would have been accepted.

**The sacrifice and the brother.**

So the twin brother of the ugly daughter said, 'Marry your sister to me and I will marry my sister to you.' He said, 'No, for I have more right to my sister.' So they both offered a sacrifice. The sacrifice of the one who offered the sheep was accepted while the sacrifice of the other (the twin brother of the beautiful daughter), which consisted of some produce, was not accepted. Qabil's brother, the pious man whose sacrifice was accepted because of his piety, said to his brother, who threatened to kill him without justification,. (Qurban), in terms of Arabic lexical usage, refers to whatever is made the medium of nearness to someone; and in Islamic legal terminology, it means the Dhabihah or sacrifice which is offered to seek nearness to Allah Ta ala. As customary with them, a fire did come from the sky and ate up the sacrifice offered by Habil - and the sacrifice offered by Qabil remained lying where it was, untouched.

28.text:
The brother answers the threat by taking away the one thing the threat can use: “If you raise your hand to kill me, I will not raise mine to kill you”. The refusal is not a lack of courage, and Abel gives his reason in the same breath: “because I fear Allah, the Lord of all worlds”. He turns his face from the fight to the One who made and owns every world, so the fear that keeps his hand at his side is the same fear that fills his heart toward his Lord. The verse therefore shows how a man who has the truth answers violence: he may keep his ground in speech, as the words about the offering were kept, but he does not lift his own hand to shed the blood of a brother, and the wrong is left to be answered by the One who sees it. The words of Abel here are kept as a model of how a believer meets the anger of a kinsman, and the whole passage around them shows what the two answers produced, since one man became a killer and the other kept his hand clean.

**The hand and the fear.**

(Even if thou stretch out thy hand against me to kill me) wrongfully, (I shall not stretch out my hand against thee to kill you) wrongfully, (lo! I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds) if I were to kill you wrongfully. Abel told Cain that he might raise his hand to murder him, but that he would not retaliate, because God had prohibited any fighting between one Muslim and another.

**The fear of Allah and the hand.**

"Verily, Allah accepts only from those who have Taqwa "If you do stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall never stretch my hand against you to kill you, for I fear Allah; the Lord of all that exists. ("If you do stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall never stretch my hand against you to kill you, for I fear Allah; the Lord of all that exists.") In addition to what has been said above, through this very word, the addressees of the Holy Qur'an are also being chastened and guided to the fact that their noble prophet, on him be the peace and blessing of Allah, who is a total Ummiyy (untaught by any human being), yet he is describing the events which took place thousands of years ago, absolutely true and correct.

**The bounty and the offering.**

Abel’s offerings from his flocks of sheep and goats were accepted by God and he was duly blessed, but Cain’s offerings of his agricultural produce were not, and he remained unblessed. One of them fought against the other and killed him out of envy and transgression, because of the bounty that Allah gave his brother and because the sacrifice that he sincerely offered to Allah was accepted. Abel said that Cain’s offering had been rejected because Cain had no heartfelt fear of God and should, therefore, reform himself instead of threatening him.

**The sacrifices and the attacker.**

After this introduction, the event relating to these two sons of Adam was put in the following words by the Holy Qur'an: ‌ ‌ ‌ that is, both of them offered their sacrifices for Allah Ta ala, but it was accepted from one of them and was not accepted from the other. ("Verily, Allah accepts only from those who have Taqwa.) who fear Allah in their actions. But if one Muslim carries out his intention, while the other remains immersed in prayer, the attacker will not only shoulder the burden of his own sin, but also that of any sin which his victim might have commmitted had he not remained patient and prayerful.

29.text:
The refusal is given its full reason, and the reason looks past the quarrel to the world to come: “I want to let you bear your sin against me along with your other sins”. Abel asks that the sin of killing him be carried by Cain together with the sins he had already gathered, so the harm done to him would not be added to his own account, and he wants to gain nothing from the confrontation. Then comes the result of that burden: “then you will be one of those destined to the Fire”. The one who slaughters his brother will stand with the weight of the first killing on his own head, and the verse names the end of it plainly. The last phrase gives the rule that binds all of this together: “And that is the reward of the wrongdoers”. The reward named belongs to those who overstep the limits of Allah, and it belongs to them without exception, so the story of two brothers ends with the statement of a law that governs everyone who kills without right.

**What the wrongdoers carries.**

"Verily, Allah accepts only from those who have Taqwa "If you do stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall never stretch my hand against you to kill you, for I fear Allah; the Lord of all that exists. "Verily, I intend to let you draw my sin on yourself as well as yours, then you will be one of the dwellers of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said – that during the time of Adam – "The woman was not allowed in marriage for her male twin, but Adam was commanded to marry her to any of her other brothers. I want you to return with the sin of wrongly killing me, together with your previous sins, and become one of those who will enter the fire of Hell on the Day of Judgement and remain there.

**What the sacrifice carries.**

One of them fought against the other and killed him out of envy and transgression, because of the bounty that Allah gave his brother and because the sacrifice that he sincerely offered to Allah was accepted. I desire that you should end up with my sin the sin of slaying me and your own sin the one that you had committed before and so become an inhabitant of the Fire whereas I do not want to end up with your sin if I were to slay you and become one of them. (ibniy Adama: the two sons of Adam) appearing in the first verse , it can be said that, for that matter, every human being, man and woman, is from the progeny of Adam and everyone can be identified as being from among the children of Adam. In those days, an open sign of a sacrifice being accepted was that a fire would come from the sky and eat up the sacrifice; and the sacrifice which was not eaten up by the fire was the sign of its remaining unacceptable.

**The shouldst and the shoulder.**

Also mentioned within this statement is the cure for the envy (hasad) of the envier (hasid), that is, when the envier sees that Allah Ta ala has given someone a particular blessing which has not been given to him, then, he should take his deprivation as a result of his own practical shortcomings and sins and think of repenting from them and correcting his or her behaviour - not that one starts wishing and worrying about ways through which the other person could be made to lose the blessing he has - because this would not bring him any gain, in fact, it will become the cause of some loss to him, for acceptability with Allah depends on Taqwa (fear of Allah). (Lo! I would rather thou shouldst bear the punishment of the sin against me and thine own sin) of shedding my blood (and become one of the owners of the Fire) of the dwellers of hell. Abel told Cain that he might raise his hand to murder him, but that he would not retaliate, because God had prohibited any fighting between one Muslim and another. But if one Muslim carries out his intention, while the other remains immersed in prayer, the attacker will not only shoulder the burden of his own sin, but also that of any sin which his victim might have commmitted had he not remained patient and prayerful.

30.text:
The story then turns on the man himself and on the inner work that made the deed possible: “Yet Cain convinced himself to kill his brother”. The soul that prompts to evil made the killing seem right to him, fair-seeming and lawful in his own eyes, and that self-persuasion is named as the step between a grudge and bloodshed. What follows is short and terrible: “so he killed him, becoming a loser”. The deed is done and the loss is stated as its fruit, a loss in this world and in the next, so the man who gained what he wanted lost what he was. The verse therefore closes the story on the loser rather than on the murdered man, and it leaves the reader with the fact that the first killing of a human being by a human being ended in nothing but loss, which is the answer to every hand that rises against a brother. The killer did not even know what to do with the body of the man he had wronged, and the earth that had been given to him to walk on had to teach him where to put his brother down, so the strength that took a life could not manage the plainest duty that followed it.

**The soul and the brother.**

Then his soul prompted him it seduced him to slay his brother so he slew him and became one of the losers by slaying him. means, his conscience encouraged him to kill his brother by making it seem like a sensible thing to do, so he killed him, even after his brother admonished him. The evil prompting soul of Cain persuaded him to wrongly kill his brother, Abel. Unable to restrain it, he told his brother openly:

**The loser and the brother.**

So the soul of the other encouraged him and made fair-seeming to him the murder of his brother; he murdered him and became one of the losers Then Allah sent a crow who scratched the ground to show him how to hide the dead body of his brother. So he killed him and because of that he became one of those who are losers in this world and the Afterlife. (But (the other's) mind imposed on him) his ego permitted him (the killing of his brother, so he slew him and became one of the losers) who deserved punishment.

**The burden the first killing left.**

The punishment for the unjustified atrocity committed by Cain against his brother was given to him not only in the Hereafter but in this very world where he was immediately plunged into misery. He set a bad example and will therefore bear that burden, as well as the burden of any person who does the same until the Day of Judgement, without any reduction in the burden of those who imitate him. There is no blood shed on earth since he killed his brother, until the Day of Resurrection, but he will carry a burden from it, for he was the first person to establish murder.

**The truth and the Children.**

And he did not know what to do with him because he was the first of the Children of Adam to die on earth and so he carried him on his back. Cain was instructed by means of a crow how to bury the dead body under the ground. It has come to us through Mujahid that Cain, after committing the murder, was afflicted by his lower leg becoming stuck to his thigh. The purpose is to bring the people to adhere to moderation and balance in this matter, for the way it is an error to cringe and back out from fighting and killing to uphold the truth and put an end to falsehood, similarly, starting to kill and fight unjustly amounts to a stock destruction of one's material and spiritual life both in the present world and in the Hereafter.

**The story and the person.**

Such a person is to some extent given the scope to do whatever he likes in this world of trial, but in the eyes of God, he is the worst sinner. In these verses, Allah Ta a1a has instructed the Holy Prophet that he should relate the story of the two sons of Adam truthfully to the people of the Book, or to the whole Ummah. Qabil's brother, the pious man whose sacrifice was accepted because of his piety, said to his brother, who threatened to kill him without justification,.

31.text:
After the killing the verse stays with the same man and with what followed the deed: “Then Allah sent a crow digging a grave in the ground for a dead crow”. The bird was scratching at the soil and turning it up with its beak and its claws, burying another crow that had died, and it did this in front of the man who did not know what to do with the body of his brother. The purpose is given in the next words: “in order to show him how to bury the corpse of his brother”. He cried, “Alas! Have I even failed to be like this crow and bury the corpse of my brother?” The outcry is the voice of a man who has been taught by a bird what his own hands could not manage, and the shame in it is not for the killing alone but for the plain helplessness that came after it. Then comes the last phrase, short and heavy: “So he became regretful”. His regret is named here, and the books keep it as the regret of a murderer over the trouble his deed left in his hands rather than over the wrong done to his brother, since a man who truly repented of the killing would not have needed a crow to teach him how to cover the dead. The verse therefore closes the story of the first murder with a lesson that nothing in the creation is too small to teach a man who has lost his way, and with a warning that regret can arrive too late to be of use.

**The brother and the blessing.**

"Verily, Allah accepts only from those who have Taqwa "If you do stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall never stretch my hand against you to kill you, for I fear Allah; the Lord of all that exists. One of them fought against the other and killed him out of envy and transgression, because of the bounty that Allah gave his brother and because the sacrifice that he sincerely offered to Allah was accepted. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that Abu Ad-Darda' said, "If I become certain that Allah has accepted even one prayer from me, it will be better for me than this life and all that in it. (Then Allah sent a crow who scratched the ground to show him how to hide the dead body of his brother. He (the murderer) said, "Woe to me! Am I not even able to be as this crow and to hide the dead body of my brother?" Then he became one of those who regretted.) Also mentioned within this statement is the cure for the envy (hasad) of the envier (hasid), that is, when the envier sees that Allah Ta ala has given someone a particular blessing which has not been given to him, then, he should take his deprivation as a result of his own practical shortcomings and sins and think of repenting from them and correcting his or her behaviour - not that one starts wishing and worrying about ways through which the other person could be made to lose the blessing he has - because this would not bring him any gain, in fact, it will become the cause of some loss to him, for acceptability with Allah depends on Taqwa (fear of Allah). For this reason, the learned among the righteous elders (salaf) have said that this verse is a shot in the arms of those who are devoted to acts of worship and do deeds in the hope of finding the pleasure of Allah. People around him asked: 'As for you, you have been busy doing your Ibadat (acts of worship) and good deeds throughout your life, why, then, would you weep?' He said, 'You are saying this and ringing in my ears is this saying of Allah Ta ala: Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Masud said: 'If I become certain that Allah Ta ala has accepted some deed of mine, then, I would not surrender this blessing even if the whole world were to turn into solid gold and pass into my possession, in fact, I would take it to be nothing as compared to that blessing.'. Allah sent a crow to dig the earth in front of him to bury another dead crow and teach him how to cover his brother’s body. If, not, he will be confronted with the problem of burying the dead body, which, even after burial, will be treated by God as not having been buried.

**What the brother carries.**

As-Suddi said that the Companions said, "When his brother died, Qabil left him on the bare ground and did not know how to bury him. 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas said, "A crow came to the dead corpse of another crow and threw sand over it, until it hid it in the ground. Then God sent forth a raven scratching into the earth digging up the soil with its beak and with its legs and throwing it up over a dead raven next to it until it completely hid it to show him how he might hide the nakedness the carcass of his brother. ’ And he became one of the remorseful for having carried him; he then dug a hole for him and covered him up. We shall proceed by explaining the words used in the text of the Qur'an following which you will have an idea of the main story, and after that we shall be talking about injunctions and rulings contained therein. A man is successful if he gives a positive response to the voice of his conscience, but if, in taking the shelter of false excuses, he suppresses the voice of his conscience, then he has failed.

**The brother and the murdered.**

The murdered brother earned forgiveness for his sins and was admitted into Paradise, while the murderer failed and earned a losing deal in both the lives. So the twin brother of the ugly daughter said, 'Marry your sister to me and I will marry my sister to you.' He said, 'No, for I have more right to my sister.' So they both offered a sacrifice. (So the soul of the other encouraged him and made fair-seeming to him the murder of his brother; he murdered him and became one of the losers.) means, his conscience encouraged him to kill his brother by making it seem like a sensible thing to do, so he killed him, even after his brother admonished him. (He said: Woe unto me! Am I not able to be as this raven) in his ability (and so hide my brother's naked corpse) in the ground? (And he became repentant) he was repentant at not being able to cover his brother's naked corpse, but not repentant for having killed him.

32.text:
The verse lifts the story of the two brothers into a law given to a whole people: “That is why We ordained for the Children of Israel that whoever takes a life”. The command is stated with its limit attached, “unless as a punishment for murder or mischief in the land”, so the taking of a life is forbidden except where the law itself takes it for a murder or for a corruption that spreads through the land. The weight of a single killing is then given in a figure that cannot be missed: “it will be as if they killed all of humanity”. One life is not a small thing that can be weighed against a grievance, because the killing of one person strikes at the safety of every person, and a society in which such killing is cheap soon has no life that is safe. The other side of the law follows in the same breath: “and whoever saves a life, it will be as if they saved all of humanity”. To keep one person alive, whether by rescue, by pardon, or by holding back a hand, is to give the whole of humanity its value again, and the two clauses together place the law on the side of life. The verse then turns to the people who had received the messengers: “Although Our messengers already came to them with clear proofs”, the proofs having been given and the road made plain, “many of them still transgressed afterwards through the land”, so the law was not broken in ignorance but in defiance. The passage therefore moves from one murder to a rule for a nation, and it leaves the reader with the plain fact that the value of a life is the value of every life.

**The person and the Israelites.**

Because of that, We ordained for the Children of Israel that if anyone killed a person not in retaliation of murder, or to spread mischief in the land - it would be as if he killed all mankind, and if anyone saved a life, it would be as if he saved the life of all mankind. And indeed, there came to them Our Messengers with Al-Bayyinat, even then after that many of them continued to exceed the limits in the land The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and do mischief in the land is only that they shall be killed or crucified, or their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and a great torment is theirs in the Hereafter Except for those who (having fled away and then) came back (as Muslims) with repentance before they fall into your power; in that case, know that Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (it would be as if he saved the life of all mankind.) Al-A'mash and others said that Abu Salih said that Abu Hurayrah said, "I entered on 'Uthman when he was under siege in his house and said, 'I came to give you my support. (That is their disgrace in this world, and a great torment is theirs in the Hereafter.)[5:33] means, the punishment We prescribed, killing these aggressors, crucifying them, cutting off their hands and feet on opposite sides, or expelling them from the land is a disgrace for them among mankind in this life, along with the tremendous torment Allah has prepared for them in the Hereafter. (He who sins in this life and was punished for it, then Allah is far more just than to combine two punishments on His servant. He who commits an error in this life and Allah hides this error and pardons him, then Allah is far more generous than to punish the servant for something that He has already pardoned.) Because of that which Cain did We decreed for the Children of Israel that whoever slays a soul for other than a soul slain or for other than corruption committed in the land in the way of unbelief fornication or waylaying and the like it shall be as if he had slain mankind altogether; and whoever saves the life of one by refraining from slaying it shall be as if he had saved the life of all mankind — Ibn ‘Abbās said that the above is meant in the sense of violating and protecting its a soul’s sanctity respectively. Our messengers have already come to them that is to the Children of Israel with clear proofs miracles but after that many of them still commit excesses in the land overstepping the bounds through disbelief killing and the like. When Sayyidna Adam and Hawwa' came to live in the world and started having children, it so happened that they had twins from every pregnancy, one of the two being a boy, while the other, a girl. Also mentioned within this statement is the cure for the envy (hasad) of the envier (hasid), that is, when the envier sees that Allah Ta ala has given someone a particular blessing which has not been given to him, then, he should take his deprivation as a result of his own practical shortcomings and sins and think of repenting from them and correcting his or her behaviour - not that one starts wishing and worrying about ways through which the other person could be made to lose the blessing he has - because this would not bring him any gain, in fact, it will become the cause of some loss to him, for acceptability with Allah depends on Taqwa (fear of Allah). Due to Cain’s murder of his brother, I informed the Israelites that any person who kills another person for no valid reason – such as legal retribution or as punishment for causing corruption in the land by treason or waging war – it is as if he has killed all people, since he did not make a distinction between an innocent and a guilty person. Similarly, when someone saves another from oppression, he is not the saviour of just one person but of all human beings, because he is protecting the principle of respect for life of all hman beings, which holds that nobody has the right to raise his hand to another.

**What the lives carries.**

The Ayah states, whoever kills a soul without justification – such as in retaliation for murder or for causing mischief on earth – will be as if he has killed all mankind, because there is no difference between one life and another. (and if anyone saved a life...) by preventing its blood from being shed and believing in its sanctity, then all people will have been saved from him, so,. So this is the meaning of saving the life of all mankind, for whoever forbids killing a soul without justification, the lives of all people will be saved from him. (and if anyone saved a life, it would be as if he saved the life of all mankind.) means, "He who does not kill anyone, then the lives of people are safe from him." Whoever refrains from killing a person whose soul I have made sacred, and regards it to be forbidden to kill such a person, it is as if he has given life to all people, because in such an action lies the safety of all people.

**The punishment and the Messenger.**

(it would be as if he killed all mankind,) "He who kills a believing soul intentionally, Allah makes the Fire of Hell his abode, He will become angry with him, and curse him, and has prepared a tremendous punishment for him, equal to if he had killed all people, his punishment will still be the same. (The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and do mischief in the land...) "Was revealed concerning the idolators, those among them who repent before being apprehended, they will still be liable for punishment for the crimes they committed." It has many lessons and good counsels for the present and future generations; and under them, mention has been made of many religious injunctions. (Our messengers came unto them) i.e. the Children of Israel (of old with clear proofs) with commands, prohibitions and signs, (but afterwards lo! many of them) the Children of Israel (became) after the messengers (prodigals in the earth) ascribing partners to Allah.

33.text:
The verse sets out the punishment for a crime against the whole community: “Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and spread mischief in the land is death, crucifixion”. The two offences named are joined, waging war and spreading corruption, because the one who raises a hand against the people of a land raises it against the law that keeps them safe, and the punishment is given in a range rather than a single form: death, or crucifixion, or “cutting off their hands and feet on opposite sides, or exile from the land”. The ruler weighs the crime and applies what fits it, so a killer is killed, a robber who takes property and life is dealt with more severely, and one who only frightens the road is driven out of the land. The verse then names what the punishment is for: “This penalty is a disgrace for them in this world”. It is not a private revenge but a public shame, the loss of standing that follows a man who has made the roads unsafe, and it is meant to be seen. The last phrase carries the matter past this world: “and they will suffer a tremendous punishment in the Hereafter”, so the shame of the earth is not the end of the account, and the one who escapes the ruler does not escape the judgment that waits. The range of the penalties is left to the ruler because the crimes differ in their harm, and the verse gives the whole scale at once so that the sentence fits the offence and the fear of it reaches every hand that would reach for a life or for the property of a neighbour. Law and the world to come are held together here, which is why the punishment is given as a deterrent and not as an outlet for anger.

**The hands and the punishment.**

That is their disgrace in this world, and a great torment is theirs in the Hereafter Except for those who (having fled away and then) came back (as Muslims) with repentance before they fall into your power; in that case, know that Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. He then ordered that their hands and feet be cut off (and it was done), and their eyes were branded with heated pieces of iron. (That is their disgrace in this world, and a great torment is theirs in the Hereafter.)[5:33] means, the punishment We prescribed, killing these aggressors, crucifying them, cutting off their hands and feet on opposite sides, or expelling them from the land is a disgrace for them among mankind in this life, along with the tremendous torment Allah has prepared for them in the Hereafter. That mentioned requital is a degradation a humiliation for them in this world; and in the Hereafter theirs will be a great chastisement namely the chastisement of the Fire. The reason is that a powerful group when it elects to break the Law given by Allah and His blessed Messenger with force, it is really at war with the government, even though they are obviously carrying out their aggression against common human beings. That they shall be killed off or be crucified or their hands and legs be cut apart from different sides or they be kept away from the land (they live in). Therefore, a group of Sahabah, Tabi in and jurists of the Muslim Ummah, by taking the word, Aw,' in the sense of choice, has taken the position that the Imam or Amir or the ruler has been legally given the choice to award all four punishments, or any one of them as suitable in their cases, of course, after an assessment of the power and terror of the robbers and the gravity or negligibility of their crimes. Here too, though this act of looting may have been performed directly only by some of them, yet the punishment will remain just the same for all of them, because whatever the doers of the act did, they did it with their trust in the cooperation and assistance of their accomplices, therefore, all of them are partners in the crime. And if they had yet to commit the crime of killing or plundering while they were arrested beforehand, their punishment is : ‌ that is, they be kept away from the land they live in. Similarly, if the position is that no one was killed, no property was looted, but, some people did receive wounds at their hands, then, they would be subjected to the law of Qisas (Even Retaliation) against the inflicting of wounds. The punishment of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, and who challenge them by spreading corruption on earth though killing, looting and creating fear on the roads, is that they be killed, or crucified, or that they have their alternate hands and feet cut off, and if the offence is repeated the left hands and right feet are to be cut off, or they are to be exiled. (The only reward) requital (of those who make war upon Allah and His messenger) of those who disbelieve in Allah and His messenger (and strive after corruption in the land) and engage in sin in the land, i.e. by wrongfully killing others and taking their properties (will be that they will be killed) He says: the punishment of one who kills and does not take the victim's property is that he be killed (or crucified) He says: the punishment of one who kills a person and also takes his property is that he be crucified, (or have their hands and feet on alternate sides cut off) the right hand and the left leg. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, ordered that they be given a flock of camels, a shepherd and commanded them to set off with them, with a dispensation to drink their milk and urine. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, sent after them and when they were captured and brought to him, he cut off their hands and feet and gouged their eyes.

**The Muslim and the Muslims.**

'Ali bin Abi Talhah said that Ibn 'Abbas said about this Ayah, 'He who takes up arms in Muslim land and spreads fear in the fairways and is captured, the Muslim Leader has the choice to either have him killed, crucified or cut off his hands and feet. As for the Muslims who commit this crime and repent before they are apprehended, the punishment of killing, crucifixion and cutting the limbs will be waved. The second point worth noticing in this verse is that Muharabah' (fighting) of the criminals is said to be against Allah and His Messenger, though the confrontation or fighting waged by robbers and rebels is apparently against human beings.

**The Messenger and the punishment.**

This Ayah does not save a Muslim from punishment if he kills, causes mischief in the land or wages war against Allah and His Messenger and then joins rank with the disbelievers, before the Muslims are able to catch him. (The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and do mischief in the land...) "Was revealed concerning the idolators, those among them who repent before being apprehended, they will still be liable for punishment for the crimes they committed." What about those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and cause mischief in the land?' So he recited the Ayah until he reached,. I repented before you had any authority over me.' Abu Musa proclaimed, 'This is so-and-so, who had waged war against Allah and His Messenger and caused mischief in the land, and he repented before we had authority over him. The first verse begins by stating the punishment of those who fight against Allah and His Messenger and go about spreading disorder in the earth. What does fighting' (Muharabah) against Allah and His Messenger and spreading disorder in the earth mean, and to whom does this apply? But, when the government itself is Islamic, a government which subscribes to and enforces the Law of Allah and His Messenger, this act of fighting' (Muharabah) will invariably be regarded as being against' Allah and His Messenger.

34.text:
The same passage that laid down the harshest penalty opens a door inside it: “As for those who repent before you seize them”. The repentance is put in its narrow place, before the power of the ruler takes hold of the offender, and the condition shows what the door is for: a man who stops and turns while he can still turn belongs to a different matter than a man who is dragged to justice. What follows from that turning is stated at once: “then know that Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful”. The right of Allah is lifted from the one who repents, and the mercy that receives him is named with both of its faces, the forgiveness that covers the wrong and the mercy that keeps him among the living. The verse does not say that the rights of the people he wronged are cancelled, since those belong to the men he robbed or killed and their families, and the books keep the two matters apart: what is owed to Allah falls away with repentance, and what is owed to a servant of Allah is settled with the servant or left to the justice of the Day. The door is therefore narrow, honest, and placed exactly where the offender still has a choice.

**The exception and the warmongers.**

Except for such warmongers and waylayers as repent before you overpower them; for know that God is Forgiving to them of what they have done Merciful to them. The exception is that should the robbers and rebels were to repent - before they are surrounded and overpowered by government forces, and are in a state when their position of strength is still operative - and decide on their own to abandon their practice of highway robbery, then, this Prescribed Punishment will stand dropped in their case. Except for those warmongers who repent before you, people of authority, get hold of them. (Save those who repent) from disbelief and idolatry (before ye overpower them) i.e. before you capture them. And indeed, there came to them Our Messengers with Al-Bayyinat, even then after that many of them continued to exceed the limits in the land The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and do mischief in the land is only that they shall be killed or crucified, or their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. Therefore, on the other hand, things have been made softer and lighter through this exception, that is, let them repent if they would, in which case, the punishment of the mortal world would also be forgiven. Al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded that Abu Qilabah 'Abdullah bin Zayd Al-Jarmi, said that Anas bin Malik said, "Eight people of the 'Ukl tribe came to the Messenger of Allah and gave him their pledge to follow Islam.

**The Messengers and the provision.**

(Save those who repent) from disbelief and idolatry (before ye overpower them) i.e. before you capture them. And indeed, there came to them Our Messengers with Al-Bayyinat, even then after that many of them continued to exceed the limits in the land The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and do mischief in the land is only that they shall be killed or crucified, or their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. In addition to that, there is a strategic advantage here in this provision, that is, it is not always easy to control or overpower a powerful group, therefore, the door of persuasion has been left open for them so that they are induced to repent. Except for those warmongers who repent before you, people of authority, get hold of them. Due to His mercy, He overlooks the punishment that is due to them.

**The world and the caravan.**

However, when a man’s righteous action brings him nearness to God, he experiences this in this world purely in the form of heavenly feeling. If then a person has killed and stolen property he should be killed and have his limbs cut off on opposite sides but not crucified — this is the more sound of two opinions held by al-Shāfi‘ī. (That is their disgrace in this world, and a great torment is theirs in the Hereafter.)[5:33] means, the punishment We prescribed, killing these aggressors, crucifying them, cutting off their hands and feet on opposite sides, or expelling them from the land is a disgrace for them among mankind in this life, along with the tremendous torment Allah has prepared for them in the Hereafter. The kind of effect it produced was that Ali Asadi who robbed passersby on the outskirts of Madīnah with the help of his group happened to hear one of those days the following verse of the Holy Qur'an being recited by a Qari in the caravan (under attack) : ‌ ‌ (0 My servants who have committed excesses against their own selves, do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah - Zumar, 39-53). This proviso is expressed without any statement to the effect ‘do not submit them to prescribed legal punishment’ to point out that when such a person repents only God’s prescribed punishments hudūd — and not those deriving from the rights of human beings — are waived.

35.text:
The verse gathers the whole of the religious life into one short sentence: “O believers, Be mindful of Allah and seek what brings you closer to Him and struggle in His Way”. Mindfulness of Allah comes first, the fear that keeps a person from the forbidden and keeps him to what he was commanded, and the seeking of nearness follows, the search for the means by which a servant approaches his Lord, in worship, in obedience, and in the good works that carry a person towards Him. The struggle in the way of Allah is named next, the effort that costs something, whether in fighting when fighting is asked or in the daily labour of holding to the command where it is hard. The three are put in one order because they belong together: mindfulness guards the road, nearness is the goal of the road, and struggle is the walking of it. The verse then gives the fruit of all three: “so you may be successful”. Success is set at the end of the sentence as its aim, not as a payment owed for the works, and the seeker is left to understand that the road itself is the mercy by which he reaches what he is promised.

**The right and the Wasilah.**

Have Taqwa of Allah and seek the Wasilah to Him, and strive hard in His cause, so that you may be successful Verily, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth, and as much again therewith to ransom themselves thereby from the torment on the Day of Resurrection, it would never be accepted of them. (When you hear the Mu'adhdhin, repeat what he says, and then ask for Salah (blessing, mercy from Allah) for me. Verily, whoever asks for Salah for me, then Allah will grant ten Salah to him. Then, ask for the Wasilah for me, for it is a grade in Paradise that only one servant of Allah deserves, and I hope that I am that servant. Verily, whoever asks (Allah) for Wasilah for me, he will earn the right of my intercession.) Allah said,. (O ye who believe!) in Muhammad and the Qur'an (Be mindful of your duty to Allah) regarding that which He has commanded you, (and seek the way of approach unto Him) seek the highest rank; it is also said that this means: seek with Him high degrees through righteous works, (and strive in His way) in His obedience (in order that ye may succeed) so that you escape His wrath and torment and so that you attain to faith.

**What the closer carries.**

O you who believe fear God fear His chastisement by being obedient to Him and seek the means to Him that obedience which brings you closer to Him and struggle in His way in order to elevate His religion; so that you might prosper triumph. As for the word, wasilah spelt with the letter, sin, it means that which brings someone closer to some-one else through liking and love. Therefore, the more particular one is in following the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet in acts of worship, transactions, dealings, morals, social living, practically in all departments of life, the more beloved of Allah one shall be, and the more widening becomes the gyre of this love, the closer and nearer to Allah one shall be.

**The that and the brings.**

The act of seeking to gain access to Allah - that is, wasilah' to Allah, to be precise - is anything which brings a servant of Allah nearer to his or her sole object of worship with all longing and love. O you who believe in Allah and follow His Messenger, be mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions, search for a means of closeness to Him by doing what He instructs you to do and staying away from what He prohibits you from, and strive against the disbelievers for His pleasure so that you get what you desire and you are saved from what you fear. However, when a man’s righteous action brings him nearness to God, he experiences this in this world purely in the form of heavenly feeling.

36.text:
The verse turns to those who rejected the messengers and states what waits for them: “As for the disbelievers”. It is not addressed to a small band but to everyone who disbelieves, and the weight of what they will try to pay is given in full: “even if they were to possess everything in the world twice over and offer it all to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Judgment”. Every treasure the earth carries, doubled, offered in one heap to buy a way out from the punishment of that Day, and the answer is given before they can hope: “it would never be accepted from them”. The ransom fails because the matter is not a debt that wealth can settle; the Day is a Day of judgment in which the scales weigh deeds and not prices, and no amount of gold can buy back a life spent in refusal. The verse closes on what remains after the ransom is refused: “And they will suffer a painful punishment”. The sentence leaves the reader with the difference between the two kinds of wealth, the wealth that is gathered in this world and the deeds that are carried to the next, since the one can be doubled without limit and the other has a fixed measure which cannot be bought. The verse speaks of what the disbelievers would wish to give, not of what they were asked to give, and the wish itself is part of the punishment, since a man who sees the price and cannot pay it knows exactly what he has lost.

**The ransom and the disbelievers.**

(Whoever, after hearing to the Adhan says, "O Allah! Lord of this perfect call and of the regular prayer which is going to be established! Grant Muhammad the Wasilah and superiority and send him [on the Day of Judgment] to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him," then intercession from me will be permitted for him on the Day of Resurrection.) After Allah commanded Muslims to avoid the prohibitions and to work towards obedience, He commanded them to fight against their enemies, the disbelievers and idolators who have deviated from the straight path and abandoned the correct religion. (Verily, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth, and as much again therewith to ransom themselves thereby from the torment on the Day of Resurrection, it would never be accepted of them. And theirs would be a painful torment.) So if a disbeliever brought the earth's fill of gold, and twice as much as that amount on the Day of Judgment to ransom himself from Allah's torment that has surrounded him, and he is certain that he will suffer from it, it will not be accepted of him. (And theirs will be a lasting torment.) meaning, eternal and everlasting, and they will never be able to depart from it or avoid it. (A man from the people of the Fire will be brought forth and will be asked, 'O son of Adam! How did you find your dwelling?' He will say, 'The worst dwelling.' He will be told, 'Would you ransom yourself with the earth's fill of gold?' He will say, 'Yes, O Lord!' Allah will say to him, 'You have lied. I asked you for what is less than that and you did not do it,' and he will be ordered to the Fire.) Muslim and An-Nasa'i recorded it. Truly as for the disbelievers if they possessed definitely all that is in the earth and the like of it with it by which to ransom themselves from the chastisement of the Day of Resurrection it would not be accepted from them; theirs shall be a painful chastisement. A deeper look into this particular style of the Qur'an would reveal that its oft-recurring approach is not simply to state the letter of the law of penalty and punishment as some cold and coercive command from the law giver and just leave it at that, instead, by taking the approach of an affectionate nourisher and nurturer, it also smooths out the edges of the human mind to prepare it for its ultimate abstention from crimes. What begins must end and this race of gold and greed will also end when the punishment of the Doomsday will appear in sight and, at that time, if these people were to offer all they had collected in the mortal world, wealth and property, things and things of comfort, taste and value, offer all of it in return for their release from the punishment, then, this would not be possible anymore. Even if the wager is increased higher, suppose everything of value were to be owned by one person, nay, let us say twice as much, and if he were to offer all of it to have his release from the punishment, still then, nothing would be accepted from him and he will not have his deliverance from the punishment of the Hereafter. Had those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers owned everything in the earth and the likeness of it and gave all of that to ransom themselves from Allah’s punishment on the Day of Judgement, such ransom will not be accepted from them. (As for those who disbelieve) in Muhammad and the Qur'an, (lo! if all) the wealth (that is in the were theirs, and as much again therewith) and double of it with it, (to ransom them from the doom on the day of Resurrection, it) the ransom (would not be accepted from them. Theirs will be a painful doom).

**The never and the theirs.**

And theirs would be a painful torment They will long to get out of the Fire, but never will they get out therefrom; and theirs will be a lasting tormen. Allah encouraged the believers by reminding them of the unending success and great happiness that He prepared for them for the Day of Resurrection, which will never change or decrease for those who join Jihad in His cause. Those who live in these dwellings will always be comfortable and will never be miserable, living, never dying, and their clothes will never grow thin, nor will their youth ever end. The more the flames lift them to the upper part of Hell, the more the angels of punishment will strike them with iron bars and they will fall down to its depths,.

**What the them carries.**

In verses previous to those cited above, the Islamic Prescribed Punishment of robbery and rebellion, as well as the details of injunctions relating to them, were mentioned while the Prescribed Punishment for theft is coming up after three verses later. It is so poignant that even a little reflection on it could bring an instant revolution in the lives of men and women of such persuasion compelling them to abandon all Kufr and Shirk and sin.

37.text:
The verse describes the condition of the people of the Fire and the thing they will want most: “They will be desperate to get out of the Fire but they will never be able to”. Their desire to leave will be the whole of their desire, and the door stays shut because the time of action has passed and what remains is only the recompense of what they did. The second phrase states how long the state lasts: “And they will suffer an everlasting punishment”, a punishment that is not interrupted by any relief and does not end with any death, and it is named here beside the wish to escape so the two are seen together, the desire that cannot reach and the punishment that cannot end. The verse sits directly after the mention of the ransom, and the order is part of the lesson: the men who would have paid the earth twice over were told that their wealth would not be accepted, and now they are shown at the edge of the Fire with nothing left to offer at all. The Fire is named as a place they will want to leave, which is itself a mercy spoken to the living, since the warning of a door that never opens is given while the door of this world is still open, and the one who hears it has not yet run out of time.

**The disbeliever and the perpetual.**

They will desire they will wish to exit from the Fire but they will not exit from it; theirs shall be a lasting a perpetual chastisement. (They will wish to come forth from the Fire) by changing one state into another, (but they will not come forth from it) from the Fire. They will want to leave the fire of Hell after they enter it. So if a disbeliever brought the earth's fill of gold, and twice as much as that amount on the Day of Judgment to ransom himself from Allah's torment that has surrounded him, and he is certain that he will suffer from it, it will not be accepted of him.

The verse answers a doubt that the preceding laws could raise in a mind that had not yet come to know Allah as He is: “Do you not know that the kingdom of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone?” The question is not asked for information but to settle a matter, and the kingdom is stated in its widest form, the heavens and the earth and what is in them, so the One who ordained the penalties is the owner of all that they touch.
